# Code guide

A map of the code of qando: where each part lives, the words it uses, what the main flows go through and, folder by folder, what each piece does and the functions it offers to the rest of the code.

## How this guide is written

The guide is one file with a strict shape, so that a person or a tool can split it into one `README.md` per folder (a mirror of the repository) and find what they need without reading the whole of it.

- **Top-level sections.** _Index_, _Glossary_ and _Flows_ describe the whole project; they become the mirror's root `README.md`, `GLOSSARY.md` and `FLOWS.md`.
- **One section per folder.** Under _Folders_, each folder of the repository has a section whose heading is its exact path (`` ### `apps/web/src/app/features/vote` ``); the section becomes that folder's `README.md`. Generated or local-only folders (`node_modules`, `dist`, `reports`, `test-results`, `.angular`, `e2e/.features-gen`, `apps/api/drizzle/meta`) have none.
- **Every folder section has the same parts, in this order**: **Summary** (one line, the one the index shows), **Purpose**, then whichever of **Contents** (sub-folders and files), **Components**, **Exports** apply, then **Depends on** and **Used by** (paths of other folders).
- **Each section stands alone.** It never says "see above"; another piece is named by its path.
- **Only the public interface.** A folder lists what other folders use (exported functions, classes, types, components with their inputs and outputs); private helpers are left to the code. An Angular component is one entry, whatever files (`.ts`, `.html`, `.scss`, `.spec.ts`) it has.
- **Kept current.** The pull request that adds, removes or changes a public piece updates its section here. `npm run check` (and so CI) fails when a folder has no section, a section names a folder that no longer exists, a section does not name an export of its folder, or a component's row does not name one of its inputs, outputs or models (`tools/guide-check`). It checks that each piece is named, not that what the guide says of it is true.

## Index

```text
.                              qando: a group finds a date that works for everyone
├── .github/                   GitHub configuration
│   └── workflows/             continuous integration (CI)
├── apps/                      the two deployable applications
│   ├── api/                   REST API (Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL)
│   │   ├── drizzle/           versioned SQL migrations
│   │   └── src/               API source: app wiring, entry points, capability tokens
│   │       ├── db/            database connection, schema, migrations, health probe
│   │       ├── email/         the emails' shared frame and templates, sent over SMTP at once or queued with retries
│   │       ├── http/          Express pieces every module shares
│   │       ├── modules/       one folder per API resource
│   │       │   ├── auth/          sign-in by email code, its email, sessions, the session request, sign-out, account deletion, the authorization server for applications, who may call the connector (Better Auth)

│   │       │   ├── date-interpretations/  read the dates and times a phrase says
│   │       │   ├── docs/          OpenAPI document and Swagger UI

│   │       │   ├── health/        GET /api/health

│   │       │   └── results/         read the results by the results link
```

## Glossary

The words of the product and the name each one has in the code.

| Term                    | In the code                                                                                                                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Event                   | `events` table, `PublicEvent`, `StoredPublicEvent`                                                                         | What an organizer creates so a group can choose a date: a title, the options, a deadline, a time zone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Organizer               | `organizerName`                                                                                                            | The person who creates the event and later confirms a date.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Account, owner          | `users` table, `ownerId`                                                                                                   | An organizer's account, created verified by the first sign-in code of an email; every event belongs to one (its owner).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Session                 | `sessions` table                                                                                                           | One signed-in browser of an account, carried by the session cookie.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Sign-in code            | `verifications` table, `SignInCodes`, `emailCodesOf`                                                                       | The 6-digit code emailed to sign in, or to delete the account (the email's one code, whatever it was sent for): only its hash is stored, valid for 10 minutes and 5 wrong tries; a new one, once delivered, replaces the last.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Participant, voter      | `participations` table                                                                                                     | Anyone who opens the participation link and votes; no account needed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Option                  | `Option`, `options` table, `optionId`                                                                                      | One thing participants answer: a whole day, a range of days (`endDate`), or a single date with a start time and optionally an end time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Vote, participation     | `Participation`, `CastVoteBody`, `MyVote`, `ValidVote`                                                                     | One participant's answer to every option of an event. Stored as a participation with one vote state per option.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Vote state              | `VoteState`: `available` · `preferred` · `unavailable`                                                                     | The answer to one option. At most one option of a vote is `preferred`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Answers                 | `Answers` (web)                                                                                                            | The vote while it is being made on the voting page, one state per option ID.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Quick vote              | `allAvailable`, `VoteWelcome.quickVote`                                                                                    | Voting every option available in one tap, without going through the steps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Named / anonymous event | `anonymous: boolean`                                                                                                       | A named event asks each voter's name (2 to 30 characters); an anonymous one never stores a name (`null`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Deadline                | `deadline`, `changeDeadlineTool` (`change_deadline`)                                                                                                                 | The last day participants can vote, a calendar date in the event's time zone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Closing instant         | `closesAt`, `closingInstant`, `closeVotingTool` (`close_voting`)                                                                                               | The last millisecond of the deadline's day in the event's time zone; voting closes then by itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Event state             | `EventState`: `open` · `closed` · `confirmed`                                                                              | Whether the event accepts votes. Always read through `currentState`, which closes an open event at its closing instant.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Confirmation            | `confirmations` table, `confirmOption`, `confirmAsAsked`, `confirmOptionTool` (`confirm_option`), `ALREADY_CONFIRMED`                                                                | The option the organizer confirmed as the date; final. Through the connector it takes two calls: the first answers what confirming would do and a code, the second, with that code once the organizer said yes, confirms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Cancelled event         | `cancelledEvents` table, `EVENT_CANCELLED`, `cancelEventTool` (`cancel_event`)                                                                                 | What is left of a cancelled event: its links answer "cancelled" with the title; it goes with the account that owned the event. Through the connector cancelling takes two calls, as confirming: the first answers what cancelling does and a code, the second, with that code once the organizer said yes, cancels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Capability token        | `newCapabilityToken`, `hashCapabilityToken`                                                                                | A random secret inside a link that grants access without an account. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Participation link      | `/vote/:eventId`, `publicId`                                                                                               | The link the organizer shares; opens the voting page. Its ID is the event's public ID.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Results link            | `/results/:resultsId`, `resultsId`                                                                                         | The link to the results page; the organizer may share it. The participation link never opens the results (`403`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Results                 | `resultsOf`, `Results`, `resultsEndpoint`                                                                                  | What the votes amount to: the winners (best attendance, then most preferred), the alternatives (as well attended, less preferred), the counts and, on named events, who answered each option each way. Provisional while voting is open, final after.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Management link         | `/manage/:eventId#t=<token>`, `openManagementLink`                                                                         | The organizer's link to manage the event; `:eventId` is the participation ID and the token travels in the fragment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Management token        | `managementTokenSchema`, `X-Management-Token` header, `management_token_hash`, `EventManagement`, `ManagementTokens` (web) | The capability to manage one event, created by the wizard's page before its first send (so a repeated send stores one event); only its hash is stored. An event an assistant creates has one the API makes and answers to no one: its owner manages it with the session. The browser that opened a management link keeps its token until it signs out.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Acting organizer        | `ActingOrganizer`, `actingOrganizer`, `ManagementCredentials`                                                              | Whoever a management request acts as, resolved once from its credentials (the management token, the owner's session) before any management use case runs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Recommended options     | `recommendedOptionIds`                                                                                                     | The options the results recommend (their winners); confirming another one asks first.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Vote-edit token         | `voteTokenSchema`, `X-Vote-Token` header                                                                                   | The capability to read and edit one vote. The voting page creates it before the first send, so a repeated send never stores a second vote.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Private link            | `/vote/:eventId/my-vote#t=<token>`, `openMyVoteLink`                                                                       | The link to edit one's own vote from another browser; carries the vote-edit token.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Endpoint, contract      | `Endpoint`, `defineEndpoint`, `endpoints`                                                                                  | One HTTP endpoint described once with its Zod schemas; the API serves it, the web calls it, the OpenAPI document is generated from it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Port                    | `PublicEvents`, `Participations`, `EventResults`, `ManagedEvents`, `NewEvents`, `DatabaseCheck`, `Sessions`, `ConnectorAccess`                                         | The interface through which an API module reaches what lies outside it (the database, the sign-in library); tests replace it with fixed answers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Step, step stack        | `Step`, `StepStack`                                                                                                        | A page made of steps shown as a stack of cards: the current card, the earlier ones folded into tabs above it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Design token            | `_tokens.scss`                                                                                                             | A named colour, size, spacing or duration; stylesheets use tokens, never literal values.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Demo event, seed        | `demoEvents`, `seedEvent`                                                                                                  | An event stored straight in the database, for local runs (`npm run db:seed`) and acceptance tests.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Session                 | `Sessions`, `sessionReader`, `signedInAccount`, `qando.session_token` cookie, `sessionEndpoint`, `Session` (web)           | A browser signed in to an account: an HttpOnly cookie Better Auth sets, valid 90 days from its last use. It manages the account's events like their management links; a change sent with it from a page of another site is refused (CSRF). The page cannot read the cookie, so it asks the API which account is signed in (`GET /api/auth/session`).                                                                                                               |
| Signed-in account       | `SignedInAccount`, `Session.account` (web), `SessionAccount` (API)                                                         | What a page knows of the account its browser is signed in as: its name (empty until it has one) and its email.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Private page            | `signedInOnly`, `signInAgainOnceEnded`                                                                                     | A page only an account signed in opens (`/my-events`, `/connected-apps`, `/profile`); anyone else is sent to sign in and comes back to it, and so is an account whose session ends while the page is open. In the API, `signedInOnly` (`apps/api/src/http`) answers `401` to a request without a session.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Connector               | `connectorPath` (`/api/mcp`), `connectorRouter`, `ConnectorAccess`, `connectorAccessOf`                                    | The address assistants call: a remote MCP server, one more way into the API's use cases, offered as tools, for the applications (AI assistants) an account allowed to act for it. Each call carries an access token the authorization server issued for the connector, and is served, for the account of that token, only while that application is still connected to the account; otherwise `401`, with where to ask for access.                                 |
| Tool                    | `Tool`, `Said`, `Refused`, `Effect`, `serverFor`, `readDatesTool` (`read_date_phrase`), `createEventTool` (`create_event`), `listEventsTool` (`list_my_events`), `readEventTool` (`read_event`), `confirmOptionTool` (`confirm_option`), `changeDeadlineTool` (`change_deadline`), `closeVotingTool` (`close_voting`), `cancelEventTool` (`cancel_event`), `votingLinkOf` | One thing an application can do through the connector for the account it acts for, with a use case of the API behind it. It answers words, which the assistant reads, and the same as data beside them, or, when it did not do what was asked, words alone that say why; it says whether a call only reads what the account has, adds to it, or changes what was there for good. Today there are eight: "Leer fechas de una frase" (`read_date_phrase`), the dates of a phrase as the wizard reads them, "Crear un evento" (`create_event`), an event created as the wizard creates it, answered with its voting link, "Ver mis eventos" (`list_my_events`), the account's events, "Ver un evento" (`read_event`), one of them with its results, "Confirmar la fecha" (`confirm_option`), the final date of one of them, in two calls, "Cambiar el plazo" (`change_deadline`), its last day to vote, and "Cerrar la votación" (`close_voting`), voting closed now, each in one call, and "Cancelar un evento" (`cancel_event`), one of them deleted for good, in two calls. An account may call tools 60 times in any minute; a call past that is answered in words with the time to wait.                                                                    |
| Test clock              | `testClock`, `X-Test-Now` header, `ScenarioClock`                                                                          | Lets an acceptance scenario set "today" for the browser and the API without touching the system clock.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Date phrase             | the `text` of `readDates` and of `DateInterpretationBody`                                                                  | What an organizer types to say when the event could take place ("todos los lunes de julio a las 20:30"), in Spanish, Catalan or English.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Date reader             | `readDates`, `@qando/date-reader`                                                                                          | Turns a date phrase into the options to mark, by rules alone: the same phrase on the same day always gives the same answer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Date interpretation     | `DateInterpretation`, `dateInterpretationEndpoint`, `POST /api/date-interpretations`                                       | What the API answers for a date phrase: the options to mark, the time questions and the notices, as an event can hold them, and what was said that no event can hold (`timesLeftOut`, `questionsNotAsked`). The phrase is copy-edited, then read by the date reader; nothing is stored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Read option             | `ReadOption`, `ReadDates`, `ReadTime`                                                                                      | One option read from a date phrase: a day or a range of days, with a time, a range of times or none. Not yet an option of an event.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Time question           | `TimeQuestion`, `ReadTime` of kind `question`                                                                              | An hour whose half of the day was not said ("a las 8"): the answer carries one question per distinct time, with its words, every date it is asked of and both readings (08:00 and 20:00), and each option of that time points at its question, for the organizer to pick.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Fragment                | `fragment` of a notice or a question                                                                                       | Words of the date phrase, quoted as written, that a notice or a question speaks of («por la tarde», «el 31 de junio»).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Notice                  | `ReadNotice`, `NoticeKind`                                                                                                 | One thing the organizer is told about a fragment of the date phrase; an answer carries every one that applies, in the phrase's order. About days that are marked, with their dates: `timeUnclear` · `tooLate` · `dayNotWritten` (midnight said of a day is the next day at 00:00). About what gave no option: `unclear` · `mismatch` · `past` (a date already past) · `pastTime` (a time of today already past) · `horizon` · `tooMany`. The reader never guesses. |
| Region                  | `region` of `readDates`                                                                                                    | The region of the organizer's browser ("ES", "US"): it says whether a date in figures ("7/4") is day/month or month/day.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Vocabulary, term        | `vocabulary()`, `Term`, `Language`                                                                                         | The words the date reader knows, language by language, each phrase with the term it means to the grammar (a weekday, a month, "every", "except"…). The grammar reads terms and never names a word.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Text editor, copy edit  | `phraseEditor`, `EditPhrase`, `CopyEdit`, `geminiEditor`                                                                   | The language model that rewrites a date phrase into a well-written one in the same language before the date reader reads it (typos, glued words, chat abbreviations, dictation). It never reads dates, has 3 seconds, and its answer is used only if it passes the edit check; otherwise the phrase is read as written.                                                                                                                                            |
| Edit check              | `keepsWhen`                                                                                                                | Whether a copy-edited phrase still says when as the phrase the organizer wrote: no number added or changed, the weekdays in their order, the only month, the negations, the week and month references, the half of the day and the meal words kept, and no weekday, month, "today", "tomorrow" or half of the day the original does not say. An edit that fails it is discarded.                                                                                   |
| Token                   | `Token`, `tokenize`                                                                                                        | A piece of a date phrase as the grammar reads it: a term of the vocabulary, a figure (a date, a clock time, a number), a pause or a word nothing reads, with its place in the phrase.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Reading                 | `Reading`, `Item`, `Expr`                                                                                                  | What a date phrase names, as said, before any calendar arithmetic: its items (a date expression with its times and exceptions) and what was not understood. The calendar turns it into options from today.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Reading rule            | `rules` in `evaluation-set.json`, `R1`…`R34` in comments                                                                   | One decision about how a date phrase is read ("a weekend gives one range option, Saturday to Sunday"), numbered; the code names the rule it applies.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Evaluation set          | `evaluation-set.json`, `evaluation-set.test.ts`                                                                            | 687 date phrases (487 in Spanish, 139 in English, 61 in Catalan), each with the day it is written on, the region and the answer expected. The agreed score is 100 %: the unit tests, and so CI, fail if one stops passing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Flows

What each user-visible flow goes through, from the page to the database. Paths are relative to the repository root.

### Open the voting page

1. The participant opens the participation link `/vote/:eventId`; the route (`apps/web/src/app`) loads **`VotePage`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/vote`).
2. `VotePage` reads the event with `apiResource(publicEventEndpoint)` (`apps/web/src/app/core/api`), which calls `GET /api/public/events/{id}` (`packages/contracts/src/public-events`).
3. The API's **`publicEventsRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/public-events`) finds the event through the `PublicEvents` port (its repository reads only what participants may see) and answers it with its current state from **`currentState`** (`packages/domain/src`). An unknown link answers `404 NOT_FOUND`, a cancelled event `410 EVENT_CANCELLED` with its title.
4. At the same time, **`MyVotes.stored`** reads the vote this browser holds for the event, if any (`GET …/participations/mine` with its vote-edit token), so the page can say "you already voted" and start from those answers.
5. A link that no longer takes votes shows **`VoteEnded`** in place of the steps: closed (saying whether this browser's vote was registered), the confirmed date, or cancelled under the kept title (`410`). A link of no event (`404`, or `400` when malformed) shows **`NotFoundCard`** (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`); only a failed request offers to try again (`ErrorState`).

### Vote

1. On **`VoteWelcome`** (step 1) the participant types a name on a named event, then either sends a **quick vote** (every option available) or chooses the dates.
2. **`VoteDays`** (step 2) and, in an event with times, **`VoteTimes`** (step 3) change the answers with the functions of `answers.ts` (`toggled`, `withPreferred`, `dayToggled`); all in `apps/web/src/app/features/vote`.
3. **`VoteConfirm`** shows what the answers amount to (`summaryOf`, `packages/domain/src`) and sends them.
4. **`MyVotes.cast`** creates the vote-edit token before the first send and sends `POST /api/public/events/{id}/participations` with it in `X-Vote-Token`.
5. The API's **`participationsRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/participations`) checks, inside one transaction that locks the event, that the event is open (`currentState`) and that the vote is valid (`validateVote`), and stores it under the token's hash (`hashCapabilityToken`, `apps/api/src/capability-token.ts`). Sending the same token again stores nothing new and gets the same answer. A closed event answers `409 VOTING_CLOSED`; an invalid vote `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with every problem; a vote answering an option the event no longer has (the organizer replaced them) `409 OPTIONS_CHANGED`.
6. **`VoteThanks`** shows the private link `/vote/:eventId/my-vote#t=<token>`.
7. A vote refused because voting closed meanwhile (`409`) makes the page read the event again (the steps stay, locked): it turns into the confirmed `VoteEnded` when the organizer confirmed a date, else (or when the read fails) into the closed one. Either says the vote did not arrive in time, or, when `MyVotes.stored` reads a vote stored before, that the changes did not and that vote is kept; a `410` turns it into the cancelled one. A vote refused because the organizer replaced the options (`409 OPTIONS_CHANGED`) also makes the page read the event again: it goes back to where the vote was sent from (the days, or step 1 after the quick vote) with the new options, the name kept and every answer available again, and says "Las opciones han cambiado: vuelve a marcar tus preferencias."; when the read fails, the send failed.

### Edit my vote

1. From the same browser, the voting page finds the stored vote (`MyVotes.stored`) and the steps start from its answers (`resumed`).
2. From another browser, the participant opens the private link: **`openMyVoteLink`** hands the token to `MyVotes.claim` and opens the voting page without the token in the address bar.
3. Sending calls `PUT /api/public/events/{id}/participations/mine` with the token; `participationsRouter` replaces the name and every state of that participation. A token of another event answers `403 FORBIDDEN`.

### Open the results

1. Anyone with the results link opens `/results/:resultsId`; the route (`apps/web/src/app`) loads **`ResultsPage`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/results`).
2. `ResultsPage` reads the results with `apiResource(resultsEndpoint)` (`apps/web/src/app/core/api`), which calls `GET /api/results/{resultsId}` (`packages/contracts/src/results`).
3. The API's **`resultsRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/results`) runs **`readResults`**: it finds the event with its votes through the `EventResults` port, works out the winners and alternatives with `resultsOf` (`packages/domain/src`) and adds the names on named events. The participation link answers `403 FORBIDDEN`, a cancelled event `410 EVENT_CANCELLED`, an unknown link `404 NOT_FOUND`.
4. The page names each option with **`OptionLabels`** and draws the bars with **`ResultsChart`**; **`ShareLinks`** (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) shares the link. A `403`, `404` or `400` shows `NotFoundCard`, a `410` the cancelled `VoteEnded`.

### Sign in with an email code

1. Without a session, **`AppHeader`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/layout`) links to `/sign-in` with the page to come back to. An application's request to connect made without a session opens the same page: the authorization server (`authorizationServerOf`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`) sends the browser to `/sign-in` with the request, signed and valid 10 minutes, as the address's query, and the page keeps it (`connectionRequestOf`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) to send it with the code. **`SignInPage`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/sign-in`) checks the email against the contract and sends it to `POST /api/auth/sign-in-code` (`packages/contracts/src/auth`). The API's **`signInRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) first refuses a request from a page of another site, or without `Origin`, with **`ownPagesOnly`** (`apps/api/src/http`): `403 FORBIDDEN`, session or not. Then **`requestLimit`** (`apps/api/src/http`) allows 20 codes an hour per client address and **`quota`** (`apps/api/src/http`), per email, a new code only after 30 seconds and at most 5 in any hour, by the API's clock (a code the email server refused gives its place back, one delivered after the browser left keeps it); beyond, `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`. A broken email answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (`contractBroken`).
2. **`SignInCodes.send`** (`emailCodesOf`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`) has Better Auth create a 6-digit code for the email, stored hashed, renders it with **`signInCodeEmail`** (the code in the subject; the account's stored name, if it has one) and hands it to the `SendEmail` port, **`smtpEmail`** (`apps/api/src/email`). The answer is `200 { sent: true, resendAfterSeconds: 30 }`; an email server that refused it or could not be reached is logged without its message and answers `502 CODE_NOT_DELIVERED`, and the page may ask again at once; the last delivered code stays the stored one until the new one is delivered, so it is still accepted with its own tries and expiry.
3. **`SignInCode`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/sign-in`), through the code step **`CodeStep`** (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`), keeps the 6 digits of what is typed or pasted and sends `POST /api/auth/sign-in` with `{ email, code }` (from the creation wizard, also the last step's name; from a sign-in page that a request to connect opened, also that request, `connectionRequest`) as soon as the sixth is in, behind the same `ownPagesOnly` check and at most 30 tries per 15 minutes per address (`429`); it shows each refusal, and asks for a new code after the wait.
4. **`SignInCodes.signIn`** has Better Auth check the code. The right one uses it up, opens a session (creating the account, already verified and with the name sent, if any, when the email has none; the API checks that name by the organizer's rule, `organizerNameProblem`, `packages/domain/src`, before trying the code) and answers `200 { signedIn: true }` with the session cookie. Otherwise `400`: `WRONG_CODE` with `attemptsLeft` (1 to 4, read from the code Better Auth stores), `CODE_EXPIRED` (it expired, was used, or was never sent) or `TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS` (void after 5 wrong tries, even for the right code). No answer is cached. After `200`, `SignInCode` has **`Session`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) ask the API for the account again (`Session.refresh`), so the header shows the account's menu, and only then `SignInPage` opens `returnTarget(returnTo)` (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`; "Mis eventos" by default) in place of itself.
5. A sign-in sent with a request to connect goes on with it. `SignInCodes.signIn` has Better Auth check the request's signature and its 10 minutes before the code is tried, so nothing is left to fail once the code is used up, and with the code taken the `200` also says where the browser goes on, `continueTo`, a path of qando's: for a valid request, the authorization server's address with what the application asked (`/api/auth/oauth2/authorize?…`, its query by **`askedAgain`**, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`); for one older than 10 minutes or not signed by the authorization server, `/connect`, the consent page's address, without a request, so connecting starts again from the application. The person is signed in either way. `SignInCode` emits `signedIn` with that address, and `SignInPage`, instead of opening `returnTarget(returnTo)`, leaves for it through **`WholeNavigation`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`): the browser's own navigation, in place of the page, as the app's router does not serve the address. The authorization server takes the request again, now with a session, and sends the browser to the consent page's address (`/connect`) with the request, or back to the application when the account had already allowed it, as in _Connect an assistant_.

### Connect an assistant

1. An application (an AI assistant qando is being added to) sends the browser to the authorization server with its request to connect: `GET /api/auth/oauth2/authorize` (`authorizationServerOf`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`), which names the application by the address of the document it publishes about itself, where it asks the browser back and what it asks for.
2. Without a session, the authorization server sends the browser to `/sign-in` with the request, signed and valid 10 minutes, as the address's query. The sign-in page (**`SignInPage`**, `apps/web/src/app/features/sign-in`) keeps the request, sends it with the code and, once signed in, leaves for the address the API answers (`continueTo`), as in _Sign in with an email code_: the authorization server's again, now with a session.
3. With a session of an account that has not allowed the application, the authorization server sends the browser to `/connect` with the signed request as the address's query; the route (`apps/web/src/app`) loads **`ConnectPage`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/connect`). The page reads the request from its address (`connectionRequestOf`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) and asks which application it names: **`ConnectionConsent.application`** sends `POST /api/auth/connecting-application` (`packages/contracts/src/auth`) with `{ connectionRequest }`, the query whole.
4. The API's **`connectingApplicationRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) answers only qando's own pages (`403`) and a session (`401`); through the `ConnectionRequests` port (`connectionRequestsOf`) it checks the request's signature and its 10 minutes and answers `200 { name, host }`, the application as it described itself, or `410 CONNECTION_REQUEST_EXPIRED`.
5. `ConnectPage` shows the application's name and host, the email of the account the session holds at each moment, not the one it held when the page loaded (`Session.account`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`: another account signed in from another tab changes the card), what the application will be able to do, and "Cancelar" and "Permitir". A page opened without a request, or with one that expired (`410`), says "Esta solicitud ha caducado" and to start again from the assistant; when the session has ended (`401`), the sign-in page takes its place with the same query, and signing in comes back with the request. When the account is gone while the card shows (signed out from another tab, or a question about the session that failed), the page asks the API again what to show, as when it opened.
6. Either button calls **`ConnectionConsent.answer`**, which sends the account's answer to the authorization server's own route, `POST /api/auth/oauth2/consent` with `{ accept, oauth_query }` (the request, whole). Its `200` says where the browser goes on (`url`), and `ConnectPage` gives that address to the browser through **`WholeNavigation`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`): the address the application asked the browser back at, with a code after "Permitir", which the application exchanges for tokens at `POST /api/auth/oauth2/token`, or with the refusal (`access_denied`) after "Cancelar". A page's address (`http:`, `https:`) opens in place of the consent page; any other is handed to an application installed on the computer while the browser stays on the consent page, where the card "Vuelve a Claude" takes the consent's place, with "Abrir Claude", which hands the same answer again if the application did not open. The answer is given once: a "Cancelar" after a "Permitir" would tell the application it was refused while the allowance stays.
7. An application the account had already allowed is not asked about again: with a session, the authorization server sends the browser from the request straight back to the application with a code, and the consent page never opens.
8. With its access token, the application calls the connector, as in _Call the connector_, until the account disconnects it, as in _Disconnect an assistant_.

### Call the connector

1. An application an account allowed (as in _Connect an assistant_) sends each request of the MCP protocol to the connector, `POST /api/mcp`, from its own server, with its access token in `Authorization`. The API's **`connectorRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/connector`) first refuses a request from a page of another site with **`noForeignPages`** (`apps/api/src/http`): `403 FORBIDDEN`, before its token is looked at. A request without `Origin`, as an assistant's server sends it, goes on.
2. The access check, the `ConnectorAccess` port (**`connectorAccessOf`**, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`), has Better Auth check the token (signed by qando, issued for the connector, not older than its hour and, when it is bound to a key, with the proof of that key for this call) and then looks for what the account allowed the application, which must be there since before the token was issued: a live connection. A call let through goes on to the connector with who calls (`Caller`): the account its token is of and the connected application. Any other call is answered `401` with where to ask for access (`WWW-Authenticate`: the address of the connector's metadata and every permission), which is also how an assistant without a token yet learns where to send the organizer to connect.
3. A call let through reaches the MCP handler, which answers it on its own, no conversation kept, with a server made for that account (**`serverFor`**, `apps/api/src/modules/connector`): `server/discover` (the 2026-07-28 revision of the protocol) or `initialize` (the 2025 ones) with the presentation of qando: its name and title, `qando`, its website (the pages' public address), its symbol as an inline icon (`icon`), which Claude can show beside the connector's views, and the text the assistant reads when it connects (`texts.server.instructions`), and the notice that the list of tools never changes, so no application needs to listen for changes (a request to listen, `subscriptions/listen` of the 2026-07-28 revision, is answered at once that there is nothing to listen for, and ended); `tools/list` with the tools, today eight, each with the shape of what it takes and of the data it answers and marked by what a call does to what the account has: `read_date_phrase`, "Leer fechas de una frase", `list_my_events`, "Ver mis eventos", and `read_event`, "Ver un evento", as tools that only read, `create_event`, "Crear un evento", as one that adds and destroys nothing, and `confirm_option`, "Confirmar la fecha", `change_deadline`, "Cambiar el plazo", `close_voting`, "Cerrar la votación", and `cancel_event`, "Cancelar un evento", as ones that change, destructive. `GET` and `DELETE` answer `405`.
4. When the organizer asks the assistant for their events, the application calls `list_my_events` (`tools/call`). `serverFor` takes one of the account's 60 calls a minute (**`quota`**, `apps/api/src/http`, on the API's clock), and **`listEventsTool`** runs the use case **`listMyEvents`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`), the one behind `GET /api/me/events`, for the account of the token: its events, newest first, each in its current state and with how many people have voted. The answer carries words for the assistant (`texts`): a line per event with its title between « » (`written`: text a person wrote, to be read as data), its state with the last day of voting, how many people have voted and the identifier of its voting link, or that the account has created no event yet. Beside the words goes the same list as data (the `MyEvent`s of `packages/contracts/src/management`), checked against the shape the tool announced before it leaves.
5. When the organizer asks the assistant how one of their events is going, the application calls `read_event` with the identifier `list_my_events` gave, and **`readEventTool`** runs the use case **`readOrganizerEvent`** (`apps/api/src/modules/results`): whether the account manages the event of that participation ID is checked first (`actingOrganizer`, `apps/api/src/modules/management`), then one read through the `EventResults` port (`ofOrganizer`) gives the event as its voting page shows it and its results as the results page works them out (`resultsOf`). The tool answers them in words and as data, with the voting link alone; another account's event is answered as one that does not exist, a cancelled one with its title.
6. When the organizer asks the assistant to create an event, the application calls `create_event` with the event as the wizard sends it (the title, the options, the deadline, the time zone, a note, anonymous voting, off when left out, and the organizer's name, which may be left out), and **`createEventTool`** runs the use case **`createEventOnce`** (`apps/api/src/modules/events`) on the API's clock: a name left out, or only spaces, is the one of the account's last event; the event is checked as the web's is (`validateNewEvent`, `packages/domain/src`) and stored for the account through the `NewEvents` port (`createOnce`), with a management token the API makes and answers to no one, its emails queued as the web's are. The same event, the same in everything it holds (title, deadline, time zone, voting with or without names, note, organizer name and options), created less than 10 minutes before (an assistant that calls again, not knowing whether its first call arrived) store nothing and answer that event; an account that created 10 events in the last hour, whatever created them, stores nothing and is told how long to wait. The answer says the event was created, its title between « », and its voting link to share, in words and as data (`{ id, title, votingLink }`), never the results link nor the management link, which reaches the organizer in the summary email. An event the web would refuse is not created: the answer says so with each problem on its own line, in the web's words where it has them, each said once.
7. When the organizer asks the assistant to confirm the final date, the application calls `confirm_option` with the event's identifier and the date by its days and time, as `read_event` gave them, and **`confirmOptionTool`** answers in two calls. The first, without a code, changes nothing: it answers that nothing is confirmed yet, the question, the notes of the web's question before confirming that apply (**`confirmationNotes`**, `packages/domain/src`: nobody voted, nobody can attend, not the recommended date, voting still open), that the confirmation is final, and a code (**`confirmationCodes`**) that holds 10 minutes for that account, application, event, date and facts. The assistant shows that to the organizer and, only once they say yes, calls again with the code: the use case **`confirmAsAsked`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) confirms as the management page does, while the facts are still those, read with the event locked. A code that does not hold confirms nothing and is answered as a new first answer with a new code.
8. When the organizer asks the assistant to change the deadline or to close voting, the application calls `change_deadline` with the event's identifier and the new last day to vote, or `close_voting` with the identifier, one call each, as both can be undone: **`changeDeadlineTool`** runs the use case **`changeDeadline`** and **`closeVotingTool`** the use case **`closeVoting`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`), as the management page does, having read the event first (**`undecidedEvent`**): an event whose date is confirmed is refused with that date, voting already closed is answered with the day it closed, and a new deadline on a closed event says that voting reopened.
9. When the organizer asks the assistant to cancel an event, the application calls `cancel_event` with its identifier, and **`cancelEventTool`** answers in two calls, as confirming: the first, without a code, deletes nothing and answers what cancelling does in the words of the web's question, that it is final, and a code (**`confirmationCodes`**, signed for cancelling) that holds 10 minutes for that account, application and event; the second, with the code, runs the use case **`cancelEvent`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) and answers the message to forward to the group.
10. A call whose arguments do not fit the tool's input is answered by the protocol's library, in words saying what does not fit, before it is counted or run. A call past the 60 in a minute is not run: it is answered as a tool answers what it did not do, in words that say how long to wait, since an assistant reads a tool's answer, not a status. A call that fails is logged as any failed request, answered the same way in fixed words, never the failure's own, and counted like any other. Asking what the connector offers is not counted.
11. No answer is cached, an event stream's neither. A body over 32 kB is refused `413`; a failure while serving, of the check or of the handler, is logged as any failed request and answered `500` in the protocol's shape; a request the protocol refuses is answered and not logged.

### Disconnect an assistant

1. In the header, **`AccountMenu`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/layout`) links to "Apps conectadas", `/connected-apps`, a private page (`signedInOnly`, as in _Open a private page without a session_); the route (`apps/web/src/app`) loads **`ConnectedAppsPage`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/connected-apps`).
2. `ConnectedAppsPage` reads the account's applications with `apiResource(connectedApplicationsEndpoint)` (`apps/web/src/app/core/api`), which calls `GET /api/me/connected-apps` (`packages/contracts/src/auth`). The API's **`connectedApplicationsRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) answers only a session (`401`) and, through the `ConnectedApplications` port (`connectedApplicationsOf`), the applications its account allowed, the newest connection first, each `{ id, name, host, connectedAt }`.
3. Each row shows the application's name, its host and the day it was connected, and "Desconectar", an **`AskFirstButton`** (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) that asks "¿Desconectar?" in its place first. With no application, the page says how to connect one and shows the connector's address with "Copiar" (**`ConnectorAddress`**, `apps/web/src/app/features/connected-apps`).
4. Its "Sí" sends `DELETE /api/me/connected-apps/{id}` (`disconnectApplicationEndpoint`, `packages/contracts/src/auth`), one request per connection at a time. `connectedApplicationsRouter` takes it only from qando's own pages (`403`) and has the port withdraw what the account allowed in that connection, with every token the application renews its access with: `200 { disconnected: true }`, or `404 NOT_FOUND` for a connection the account does not have (disconnected already, or connected again under a new connection, from another tab; or another account signed in there): the row leaves too, and the page reads the list again to show what the account has now.
5. On `200` or `404` the row leaves and the focus goes to the card's heading. The application's next call to the connector is answered `401`, as `connectorAccessOf` (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) finds no live connection (as in _Call the connector_), and its next renewal is refused; connecting it again starts over, as in _Connect an assistant_. A `401` to either request means the session ended: the page goes to the sign-in page, which comes back to "Apps conectadas" (`signInAgainOnceEnded`, as in _Open a private page without a session_). Any other failure keeps the row, and the toast says "No se ha podido desconectar. Inténtalo de nuevo." (`Toaster`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`).

### Know who is signed in

1. When the app starts, **`Session`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) calls `GET /api/auth/session` (`packages/contracts/src/auth`) through `ApiClient` (`apps/web/src/app/core/api`): the page cannot read the session cookie itself.
2. The API's **`sessionRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) answers a request without the cookie `200 null` with no database work (`Sessions.carried`, `apps/api/src/http`). With the cookie it reads the session through the `Sessions` port (`sessionsOf`), sends back the cookie renewed while reading it and answers `200 { name, email }`, or `200 null` for a session that expired or was signed out; never `401`, never cached. A session that could not be read answers `500`.
3. `Session.account` is `undefined` until that answer, then the account or `null`; a request that failed counts as no session, and is asked again the next time a page needs to know (`Session.signedIn`).
4. **`AppHeader`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/layout`) shows **`AccountMenu`** for an account, the "Entrar" icon for `null`, and neither while `undefined`, so "Entrar" never shows for a moment to someone signed in.

### Open a private page without a session

1. The routes `/my-events`, `/connected-apps` and `/profile` (`apps/web/src/app`) run the guard **`signedInOnly`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`), which waits for `Session.signedIn()`.
2. With an account signed in the page opens. Otherwise the guard redirects to `/sign-in?returnTo=<the page asked for>` (`signInFrom`), and signing in comes back to that page (`returnTarget`), as in _Sign in with an email code_.
3. A session can also end while a private page is open (signed out from another tab, expired): the API then answers the page `401`. "Mis eventos" (`MyEventsPage`, `apps/web/src/app/features/my-events`) and "Apps conectadas" (`ConnectedAppsPage`, `apps/web/src/app/features/connected-apps`) call **`signInAgainOnceEnded`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) when they are created: once the page says its session ended, `Session.refresh` asks the API again, so the header shows "Entrar", and the sign-in page opens with `returnTo` set to that page, unless the user has left it meanwhile.

### Sign out

1. In the header, **`AccountMenu`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/layout`) opens from the round button with the account's initial; "Cerrar sesión" closes the menu and calls **`Session.signOut`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`).
2. `Session.signOut` sends `POST /api/auth/sign-out` (`packages/contracts/src/auth`); the API's **`signOutRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) deletes the session, then clears its cookies.
3. Only after that `200` the browser forgets the account (`Session.account` is `null`) and every management token it keeps (**`ManagementTokens.forgetAll`**), also those of other accounts' events opened there: a shared computer keeps no way into anyone's events, and the links stay in their emails. The voters' vote-edit tokens are kept.
4. `AccountMenu` opens the home page and shows the toast "Has cerrado sesión." (`Toaster`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`); the header shows "Entrar" again.
5. When the server could not end the session (`500`, or the request did not get through), `Session.signOut` rejects with nothing forgotten: the page stays as it is, still signed in, and the toast says "No se ha podido cerrar sesión. Inténtalo de nuevo."

### Delete my account

1. In the header, **`AccountMenu`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/layout`) shows a trash at the end of the email's row ("Eliminar mi cuenta", the wizard's grey trash, `trash-button`); pressing it closes the menu, the focus back on its button, and opens **`AccountDeletion`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/layout`) in a `Dialog` (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`): "¿Eliminar tu cuenta?", what goes with it and that a code goes to the account's email.
2. "Enviar código" calls **`Session.sendDeletionCode`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`), which sends `POST /api/me/deletion-code` (`packages/contracts/src/auth`). The API's **`accountDeletionRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) takes only a session from qando's pages (`401`, `403`), applies the sign-in's limits (`429`), and asks the **`AccountDeletion`** port (`emailCodesOf`) to email the account the email's one code, the sign-in's, with **`deletionCodeEmail`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`); a delivery that failed answers `502`, and the dialog says "No se ha podido enviar el código. Inténtalo de nuevo.".
3. The dialog shows **`CodeStep`** (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) in its look: the last digit calls **`Session.deleteAccount`** (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`), which sends `POST /api/me/deletion { code }`. The port checks the code with Better Auth (a wrong try counted) and **`deleteAccount`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) deletes, in one transaction, the account, its sessions, what it allowed applications to do, its events with everything under them, what is left of the events it cancelled and the code; the API answers `200 { deleted: true, events }` and clears the cookies. A wrong, expired or void code answers `400` and `CodeStep` says so, as when signing in. While the code is checked the `Dialog` is `held`: neither "Volver", the scrim nor Escape close it; a deletion unanswered after 20 seconds counts as a check without an answer ("No se ha podido comprobar el código.", "Reintentar"), and the dialog can be left again.
4. After that `200` the browser forgets the account and every management token it keeps, as when signing out, and tells its other tabs; the header drops the account's menu (and the dialog with it), the home page opens and the toast says "Se han eliminado tu cuenta y tus eventos." ("Se ha eliminado tu cuenta." with none). Each deleted event's links open "Página no encontrada".
5. When the server knows no session any more (`401` to either request: the session ended, or a deletion whose answer was lost went through and a try again finds none), `Session` forgets it the same way and the home page opens with the toast "Se ha cerrado tu sesión. Si al volver a entrar no ves tus eventos, tu cuenta ya se eliminó.".

### Create an event

1. On the home page, **`CreatePage`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/create`) holds every step's answers, kept in the tab's `sessionStorage` so a reload finds them (`openingDraft`, `keepDraft`, `wizard-draft.ts`): the title (**`WizardDetails`**), the dates (**`WizardDates`**), their times and summary (**`WizardTimes`**, **`WizardSummary`**) and the last step's (**`WizardFinish`**): the deadline, suggested by `suggestedDeadline` (`packages/domain/src`) until it is chosen in **`DeadlineField`**, a note, anonymous voting and the organizer's name (**`OrganizerNameField`**, which, empty for an organizer signed in, fills it with the organizer name of the account's last event, `GET /api/me/organizer-name`, which the page keeps with that account's email while the wizard is that account's).
2. Without a session, **`WizardFinish`** first asks for the email and sends it a code (`POST /api/auth/sign-in-code`); the code, typed on the step in place of its fields, signs in as in _Sign in with an email code_ (the last step's name for a new account), and the event is then sent as for an organizer signed in. An event sent once the session has ended is answered `401`, and the account's email is sent a code the same way. While a code is waited for, `CreatePage` keeps it in the draft and the other steps closed.
3. For an organizer signed in (`Session`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`), "Crear" sends `POST /api/events` (`packages/contracts/src/management`) through `ApiClient` (`apps/web/src/app/core/api`) with the session cookie and, in `X-Management-Token`, the event's management token (`newCapabilityToken`): the one it was last sent with when the event has not changed since (`SentEvent`, held by `CreatePage`, so "Reintentar" and a visit to another step repeat it), a new one for an event that changed: every option the dates propose (`proposedOptions`), the browser's time zone, the deadline, the note and anonymous voting. Meanwhile the step stack is locked.
4. The API's **`createEventRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/events`) checks the session and hands the event to the use case **`createEvent`**, which checks it (`validateNewEvent`, `packages/domain/src`) and stores it for the session's account with the token's hash (`NewEvents`), its emails queued to the account in the same transaction (`apps/api/src/email`): the summary, due at once (`scheduleEmail`), and "voting closed", due a minute after voting closes (`scheduleVotingClosed`); it answers `201 { participationId, resultsId }`; the outbox the API runs sends it within about 30 seconds (`composeEventEmail`). A send that repeats the token of an event of the same account (its first answer was lost) stores nothing and answers that event again; the token of another account's event is refused (`MANAGEMENT_TOKEN_TAKEN`).
5. The page keeps the management token it sent in this browser (**`ManagementTokens`**, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) and shows **`CreateDone`** in the place of the steps: the participation link to share, the day the results come, "Gestionar evento" (the management page, `/manage/` and the participation ID, which opens with that token) and "Crear otro evento". Any failure keeps the wizard as it was and offers "Reintentar".

### Open the management page

1. The organizer opens the management link `/manage/:eventId#t=<token>`; the route (`apps/web/src/app`) runs **`openManagementLink`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/manage`), which hands the token to **`EventManagement`** (kept per event by **`ManagementTokens`**, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`: in the browser's storage, until it signs out) and opens the page again without it, replacing the entry in the history. Without a token the page opens as it is, with the token the browser held before, if any.
2. **`ManagePage`** reads the event with `EventManagement.read`, which calls `GET /api/events/{id}` (`packages/contracts/src/management`) with the stored management token in `X-Management-Token`; the browser also sends the session cookie, if it is signed in.
3. In front of the management routes, **`sessionReader`** (`apps/api/src/http`) reads the session cookie through the `Sessions` port (`sessionsOf`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`) and sends back the cookie Better Auth renewed. The API's **`managementRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) runs **`readManagedEvent`**, which first resolves the acting organizer with **`actingOrganizer`** from the token and the signed-in account: neither answers `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` without touching the database; credentials that do not manage the event (another event's token, any other link, the session of another account, an unknown event) `403 FORBIDDEN`; a cancelled event `410 EVENT_CANCELLED` with its title.
4. With the organizer resolved, the `ManagedEvents` port reads the event with its votes; the answer carries the current state (`currentState`), the vote count, the recommended options (`resultsOf`, `packages/domain/src`) and the state of each email queued to the organizer (the summary first), never cached. Every management endpoint shares the voting endpoints' rate limit.
5. The page shows the title and state, **`FinalDate`** (the choice of the final date, or the confirmed one), **`EventDeadline`** (until a date is confirmed), **`EventLinks`**, **`EventEmails`** (each email's state) and **`CancelEvent`**; `401` (no stored management token and no live session, as when the session ended after opening the event from "Mis eventos") sends the organizer to `/sign-in` with the page to come back to, in place of the page in the history, also when the session ends while the page is open (any of its requests answered `401`); `403` and a malformed ID (`400`) show "No tienes acceso a este evento", a `410` the cancelled card (`VoteEnded`, `apps/web/src/app/features/vote`) with the message to forward; only a failed request offers to try again.

### Confirm the final option

1. On the management page, **`FinalDate`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/manage`) confirms the chosen option at once in the usual case (voting closed, a recommended option, votes in); otherwise its question (`Dialog`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) first says what makes it unusual, the notes of **`confirmationNotes`** (`packages/domain/src`) that the connector says too: nobody voted, nobody can attend any option, not the recommended option, voting will close.
2. **`EventManagement.confirm`** calls `POST /api/events/{id}/confirmation` (`packages/contracts/src/management`) with `{ optionId }` and the management token in `X-Management-Token`.
3. The API's **`managementRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) runs **`confirmOption`**, which resolves the acting organizer with **`actingOrganizer`** first (`401`, `403`, `410` as when reading the event). With the session, `sessionReader` (`apps/api/src/http`) first refuses a confirmation sent from a page of another site, or without `Origin`, with `403 FORBIDDEN`.
4. In one transaction (`ManagedEvents.change`), `confirmOption` (the contract has read the option ID in lower case) locks the event (`EventChange.lock`: votes being stored finish first, later ones wait and then find voting closed) and checks it: another option confirmed already answers `409 ALREADY_CONFIRMED`, the same option again changes nothing, an option that is not the event's (the options were replaced meanwhile) `409 OPTIONS_CHANGED`. Otherwise `EventChange.confirm` stores the confirmation and the `confirmed` state, and drops the "voting closed" email unless it was sent (`dropUnsentVotingClosed`, `apps/api/src/email`): it would ask to choose the date.
5. The answer is the event as the management page shows it, read by `readManagedEvent`; the page then shows the confirmed date. A `409` (the event changed meanwhile) makes `EventManagement` read the event again, so the page shows the date confirmed meanwhile, or, when the options were replaced (`OPTIONS_CHANGED`), the new options with the amber notice "No se ha confirmado la fecha: …" at the top of `FinalDate`; a send that fails says so under the button. From then on the participation and results pages show the confirmed option and votes are refused with `409 VOTING_CLOSED`.

### Retry a failed email

1. On the management page, **`EventEmails`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/manage`) shows a failed email as "Envío fallido" with "Reintentar"; pressed, **`EventManagement.retry`** calls `POST /api/events/{id}/emails/{type}/retry` (`packages/contracts/src/management`), no body, with the management token in `X-Management-Token` (the browser also sends the session cookie, if it is signed in). Any client of the management endpoints can call it the same way.
2. The API's **`managementRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) runs **`retryEmail`**, which resolves the acting organizer with **`actingOrganizer`** first (`401`, `403`, `410` as when reading the event).
3. **`ManagedEvents.retryFailedEmail`** calls **`retryFailedEmail`** (`apps/api/src/email`), which makes the failed email due again now for one more attempt; an email that was sent, is still being tried or was never queued answers `409 EMAIL_NOT_FAILED`.
4. The answer is the email's state, `pending`; the outbox sends it at its next run, and if it fails again it is failed at once.
5. `EventEmails` hands the page the event with the email in that state, being sent ("Enviando…"), and moves the keyboard's focus to it (after a `409` or `400`, retried meanwhile from another tab, `EventManagement` reads the event again); while an email is being sent, `EventEmails` reads the event again every 10 seconds, so the page shows it sent, or failed again, without reloading.

### Cancel an event
