1. On the management page, **`CancelEvent`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/manage`) asks with `Dialog`; accepted, **`EventManagement.cancel`** calls `DELETE /api/events/{id}` (`packages/contracts/src/management`, `cancelEventEndpoint`) with the token in `X-Management-Token` (and the session cookie).
2. The API's `managementRouter` runs the use case `cancelEvent` (`apps/api/src/modules/management`), which deletes the event's row through `ManagedEvents.cancel` (options, votes, the confirmation and the queued emails go with it) and keeps its title behind its links (`cancelled_events`) in one transaction, answering `200 { title }`; a repeat, or any management credential on a cancelled event, answers `410` with the title.
3. The page shows the cancelled `VoteEnded` with the message to forward and `ShareLinks`; the participation and results links show "Este evento ha sido cancelado" under the title.

### Change the deadline or close voting

1. On the management page, **`EventDeadline`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/manage`) sends the day chosen in its selects ("Cambiar plazo", or "Reabrir votación" once closed) with **`EventManagement.changeDeadline`**, or closes voting with **`EventManagement.closeVoting`** once its question (`Dialog`) is accepted; any client of the management endpoints can call them the same way: `PATCH /api/events/{id}/deadline` with `{ deadline }` (`changeDeadlineEndpoint`, `packages/contracts/src/management`) or `POST /api/events/{id}/close` (`closeVotingEndpoint`), with the token in `X-Management-Token` (or the owner's session from a page of qando).
2. The API's `managementRouter` runs **`changeDeadline`** or **`closeVoting`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`), which resolve the acting organizer (`401`, `403`, `410`) and, in one transaction, lock the event (`EventChange.lock`): a confirmed event answers `409 ALREADY_CONFIRMED`.
3. The new closing comes from the domain (`packages/domain/src`): **`deadlineClosing`** opens voting until the end of the chosen day in the event's time zone, any day from today to twelve months ahead (`deadlineProblem`: `400` with `DEADLINE_PAST` or `DEADLINE_TOO_FAR`), so a closed event reopens; **`closingNow`** closes it now, the deadline becoming today, and gives nothing once voting has closed, so a repeat answers as the first time and changes nothing.
4. `EventChange.setClosing` stores it and queues "Votación cerrada" for that closing (`scheduleVotingClosed`, `apps/api/src/email`): due a minute after it, also when one was sent for an earlier closing. The answer is the event as `GET` reads it.
5. `EventDeadline` hands the page the event as it comes back (a `409`, confirmed meanwhile, makes `EventManagement` read it again); a new deadline is told in a toast, and after closing the keyboard's focus goes to "Reabrir votación".

### Replace the options

1. Any client of the management endpoints calls `PUT /api/events/{id}/options` (`replaceOptionsEndpoint`, `packages/contracts/src/management`) with the whole new list of options, as on creation, and `replacesOptionIds`, the IDs of the options it started from, with the token in `X-Management-Token` (or the owner's session from a page of qando).
2. The API's `managementRouter` runs **`replaceOptions`** (`apps/api/src/modules/management`), which resolves the acting organizer (`401`, `403`, `410`) and, in one transaction, locks the event (`EventChange.lock`: a vote being stored finishes first). The first that applies answers `409`: a confirmed event `ALREADY_CONFIRMED`, a closed one `VOTING_CLOSED` (moving the deadline reopens it), an event with votes `VOTES_EXIST`, options other than the ones the client started from `OPTIONS_CHANGED` (another tab saved first); then options that break a rule of a new event's options answer `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with every problem (`validateOptions`, `packages/domain/src`, today in the event's time zone).
3. Otherwise `EventChange.replaceOptions` stores the new list in chronological order with new IDs; the links stay the same. The answer is the event as `GET` reads it.
4. A vote or an edit sent from a page loaded before answers `409 OPTIONS_CHANGED` (`participationsRouter`, `apps/api/src/modules/participations`), as does a confirmation of an option replaced meanwhile.
5. In the web, **`OptionsEditor`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/manage`), at `/manage/:eventId/options`, reads the event (`EventManagement.read`), offers its options still to come in the wizard's dates and times steps, and saves with `EventManagement.replaceOptions`, which sends this request with the IDs of every option the event had; the management page opens it with "Editar opciones", beside "Confirmar fecha" in `FinalDate` (off, with why under it, once someone voted or voting is over). `saved` takes the organizer back to the management page with a message, any other answer back there too, where the page shows why: a save refused because someone voted or the options were replaced meanwhile is told once in the amber box of `FinalDate` (`backToManagement`).

### Read a date phrase

Both sides are built: the smart calendar's box of the dates step (`PhraseBox`, `apps/web/src/app/features/create`) sends the phrase and leaves what it gives on the calendar, after asking about each time said without its half of the day (`TimeQuestions`).

1. The web's **`PhraseReader`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/create`) sends `{ text, timeZone, region }` to `POST /api/date-interpretations` (`packages/contracts/src/date-interpretations`): the phrase (1 to 120 characters), the time zone it is written in and, optionally, the region of the browser's language.
2. The API's **`dateInterpretationsRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/date-interpretations`) first refuses a request from a page of another site, or without `Origin`, with **`ownPagesOnly`** (`apps/api/src/http`): `403 FORBIDDEN`. Then **`rollingHourLimit`** (`apps/api/src/http`) allows 20 phrases in any hour per client address; beyond, `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`. Only then is the body read: one that breaks the contract answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (`contractBroken`). A refused request never reaches the language model.
3. The router hands the phrase, the time zone and the region to **`InterpretPhrase`** (`phraseInterpreter`, `apps/api/src/modules/date-interpretations`), asking for the copy edit: **`EditPhrase`** (`phraseEditor`, `apps/api/src/phrase-editor`) asks the language model for a copy edit of the phrase, with a limit of 3 seconds; when the model is slow, fails or writes an edit that fails the edit check, it answers the phrase as written. A caller that leaves the copy edit out gets the phrase read as given, and the model is not asked.
4. The interpreter takes today (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and the time now (`HH:MM`) from the clock in the request's time zone and reads the phrase with **`readDates`** (`packages/date-reader/src`), and keeps what an event can hold of the reading (**`heldReading`**): a time range no event can hold (within one clock hour, or ending on the next day) is left out of its day, a question one of whose readings it cannot hold says which (`leftOut`), and a question neither of whose readings it can hold is not asked.
5. The answer is `200 { options, questions, notices, timesLeftOut, questionsNotAsked }`, never cached. Every phrase gets one: what is not understood comes as notices, never as an error. The phrase is neither stored nor logged.
6. The web's **`PhraseBox`** (`apps/web/src/app/features/create`) works out what the reading leaves chosen (`markingOf`) and the lines that tell about it (`noticeLines`): it marks every time the reading gives and decides nothing of what an event can hold; a reading picked that the reading says no event can hold leaves its days whole and is told (`timesLeftOut`). A reading that asks about a time said without its half of the day ("a las 8") first shows its questions in the box (**`TimeQuestions`**), and is worked out with the answers once the last one is given. A reading with dates goes to **`WizardDates`** through `marked`: the dates take the place of those chosen, the box closes, the calendar goes to the month of the first day marked (`firstMarked`) and the lines show above it (`NoticeBox`); when dates were chosen before, a message at the bottom of the screen says how many were replaced and offers to put them back (`Toaster.offer`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`). A reading with none stays in the box with its lines, and a phrase left unread (`PhraseRead`: `failed`, `limited`) with a red line.

### Check the service

1. Render's health check (`render.yaml`) and the smoke feature (`e2e/features/smoke.feature`, through the web's address, which forwards `/api`) call `GET /api/health` (`packages/contracts/src/health`).
2. **`healthRouter`** (`apps/api/src/modules/health`) asks the database with `SELECT 1` through `createDatabaseCheck` (`apps/api/src/db`) and answers `200` with `database: up` or `503` with `database: down`.
3. The same feature checks that the web's address forwards `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, each with or without a path after it, to the API (`render.yaml`, `proxy.conf.json`): an assistant connecting to qando looks for its two discovery documents there. The API answers the connector's metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, with or without the connector's path (`/api/mcp`) after it, and the authorization server's at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/auth` (`authorizationServerOf`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`); each document names its addresses under the site it was asked of, which the feature checks, so it holds here and deployed. `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` without the server's path is no document's address: the API answers `404`, where the web's own pages would answer `200`. It also calls the connector (`/api/mcp`) through the web's address without a token, as an assistant does before it connects: the `401` must come back with its `WWW-Authenticate` header unchanged, naming the connector's metadata under the same site and every permission to ask for, or the assistant never finds where to connect.

### Delete what qando no longer keeps

1. Once an hour, `apps/api/src/main.ts` runs **`deleteExpired`** (`apps/api/src/retention`) with the real clock (never under the test clock).
2. In one transaction it deletes the events 6 months past their date (the confirmed option's last day, or the deadline, in the event's time zone) with their options, votes, confirmation and emails, what is left of the events cancelled 6 months ago, and then, through **`deleteNoLongerKept`** (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`), the accounts left with no event and unused for 6 months (`users.last_seen_at`, which **`createAuth`**'s session hooks set on each sign-in and each daily renewal), the expired sign-in codes and sessions, and what applications were given that Better Auth can no longer take: refresh and access tokens past their expiry, the applications nobody is connected to that no request named for a day, and the proofs of signed requests past their expiry.
3. A deleted event's participation and results links show `NotFoundCard` (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`), which says events are deleted 6 months after their date; its management link is refused (`403`), as a link of no event is, and the management page's lock card says the same; it leaves "Mis eventos".

### Delete one participant's vote on request

1. A participant asks `privacidad@qando.app` to delete their vote, sending their edit link (`/vote/:id/my-vote#t=<token>`), or the event's link and their name. Someone runs `npm run db:delete-participant -- <link> [name]` (`apps/api/src/delete-participant.ts`) against the database, first without `--yes`.
2. **`readScriptArguments`** (`apps/api/src/retention`) reads the link and the name; **`deleteParticipant`** finds the one vote the request identifies: an edit link its own vote, a name the event's one vote with that name (**`sameVoterName`** of `packages/domain`), none on an anonymous event. Without `--yes` it only says which vote it found; with it, it deletes that participation, and its answers go with it.
3. **`describeDeletion`** says the outcome, or why no vote was deleted (no event has the link, the event was cancelled, no vote or several match). The voter's browser then finds no vote for its token: the voting page opens empty, and the edit link shows that it holds no vote.

### Store demo and test events

1. `npm run db:seed` (`apps/api/src/seed.ts`) or an acceptance scenario (`e2e/steps`) calls **`seedEvent`** through `openSeeder` (`apps/api/src/seed`).
2. `seedEvent` writes the event, its options, votes and outcome in one transaction and returns its links; `storedVotes` reads the votes back and `storedRows` what is left of an event, for the tests to check.

## Folders

### `.`

**Summary:** qando: a group finds a date that works for everyone.

**Purpose:** The organizer proposes dates and times and shares a link; participants vote without creating an account; the organizer reads the results and confirms the date. The repository is an npm workspace: two applications, three packages and the acceptance tests.

**Contents:**

- `apps/`: the API and the web app.
- `packages/`: the contract and the business rules both applications share, and the reader of dates written in plain language.
- `e2e/`: acceptance tests.
- `tools/`: scripts that check the repository.
- `docs/`: planning and design documents, including this guide.
- `.github/`: continuous integration.
- `package.json`: the workspaces and the scripts that run over all of them (`build`, `test`, `mutation`, `e2e`, `check`, `check:guide`, `check:references`).
- `tsconfig.base.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `stryker.base.mjs`: settings every workspace extends.
- `render.yaml`: the deployment on Render.

**Depends on:** —

**Used by:** —

### `.github`

**Summary:** GitHub configuration.

**Purpose:** Holds what GitHub runs on the repository.

**Contents:** `workflows/`.

**Depends on:** —

**Used by:** —

### `.github/workflows`

**Summary:** Continuous integration (CI).

**Purpose:** `ci.yml` runs three jobs on every pull request and push: format, lint, type-check, unit and integration tests and the build; the acceptance tests against a PostgreSQL service; and mutation testing, one job per workspace, failing below its threshold. The two longest run in parallel parts (`STRYKER_PART`), each held to the threshold on its own: the web's in twelve (files listed in `apps/web/stryker.config.mjs`, which refuses a run whose number of parts is not its own) and the date reader's in five (`packages/date-reader/stryker.config.mjs`, which refuses the same); one check for each, _Mutation testing (apps/web)_ and _Mutation testing (packages/date-reader)_, passes when all its parts do. Every night at 03:23 UTC (scheduled runs at the start of an hour are delayed or dropped), and when started by hand, it runs the mutation testing alone, of every mutant (`--force`), and saves the reports the next incremental runs start from.

**Contents:** `ci.yml`.

**Depends on:** `apps`, `packages`, `e2e` (through the npm scripts).

**Used by:** —

### `apps`

**Summary:** The two deployable applications.

**Purpose:** The API and the web app, deployed separately; the web reaches the API under `/api`.

**Contents:** `api/`, `web/`.

**Depends on:** `packages/contracts`, `packages/domain`.

**Used by:** `e2e`.

### `apps/api`

**Summary:** REST API (Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL).

**Purpose:** Serves every endpoint of the contract, stores events and votes in PostgreSQL with Drizzle, and enforces the business rules whatever the client sends.

**Contents:**

- `src/`: the source.
- `drizzle/`: the SQL migrations.
- `drizzle.config.ts`: where drizzle-kit reads the schema and writes migrations.
- `vitest.config.ts`, `vitest.stryker.config.ts`, `stryker.config.mjs`: unit tests and mutation testing.

**Depends on:** `packages/contracts`, `packages/date-reader`, `packages/domain`.

**Used by:** `apps/web` (over HTTP), `e2e` (seeds events through `apps/api/src/seed`).

### `apps/api/drizzle`

**Summary:** Versioned SQL migrations.

**Purpose:** Each schema change in `apps/api/src/db/schema.ts` becomes a numbered SQL file here (`npm run db:generate --workspace @qando/api`), reviewed in its pull request and applied in order before every deploy.

**Contents:** `0000_baseline.sql` to `0009_signing_keys_oauth_tables.sql`, one numbered file per schema change; `meta/` (drizzle-kit's journal, generated).

**Depends on:** `apps/api/src/db`.

**Used by:** `apps/api/src/db` (`runMigrations`).

### `apps/api/src`

**Summary:** API source: app wiring, entry points and capability tokens.

**Purpose:** Builds the Express app from its modules and its edges (database ports, sessions, sign-in codes, the authorization server for applications, who may call the connector, the editor of date phrases, clock, error log), and starts it.

**Contents:** `db/`, `email/`, `http/`, `modules/`, `phrase-editor/`, `retention/`, `seed/`, `test/`; the files below.

**Exports:**

| Export                                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createApp(dependencies)` (`app.ts`)                 | Builds the Express app: mounts health, the authorization server for applications (before every router that reads a body: its token route takes a form, which Better Auth reads itself), sign-in, sign-out, the session request, the account's deletion, the application a request to connect names, the connector (given `managedEvents`, the phrase interpreter, `newEvents` and the clock, which its tools run the API's use cases with, and `publicUrl`, which it names as qando's website), date interpretations (the phrase interpreter, `phraseInterpreter(editPhrase, now)`, is built once and given to both), one rate limit shared by every capability endpoint (the session reader behind it on management), public events, participations, results, management, the account's events, creating an event, docs and the error boundary, in that order.                                                                                                                                              |
| `AppDependencies` (`app.ts`)                         | The app's edges: `checkDatabase`, `publicEvents`, `participations`, `results`, `managedEvents`, `newEvents` (the `NewEvents` port of `apps/api/src/modules/events`, which the web and the connector create events through), `sessions` (the `Sessions` port), `signInCodes` (the `SignInCodes` port), `accountDeletion` (the `AccountDeletion` port), `authorizationServer` (the Express handler of the routes an application is allowed to act for an account through and of their metadata, `authorizationServerOf` of `apps/api/src/modules/auth`), `connectionRequests` (the `ConnectionRequests` port of `apps/api/src/modules/auth`, the requests to connect the authorization server signed), `connectorAccess` (the `ConnectorAccess` port of `apps/api/src/modules/connector`, who may call the connector: the check of the access token each request carries, `connectorAccessOf` of `apps/api/src/modules/auth`), `connectedApplications` (the `ConnectedApplications` port of `apps/api/src/modules/auth`, "Apps conectadas": the applications each account connected, and disconnecting one, `connectedApplicationsOf`), `editPhrase` (the copy edit of a date phrase, `EditPhrase` of `apps/api/src/phrase-editor`, which `apps/api/src/modules/date-interpretations` calls), `now` (the clock), `publicUrl` (the public address of the pages, qando's website as the connector names it), `confirmationSecret` (the secret the connector's confirmation codes are signed with; `main.ts` gives it the sign-in secret, from which the codes derive a key of their own) and `logError`. |
| `newCapabilityToken()` (`capability-token.ts`)       | A new capability token: 128 random bits in base64url (22 characters, safe in a link).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `hashCapabilityToken(token)` (`capability-token.ts`) | What is stored of a token: its SHA-256 in hex, so a copy of the database opens nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Entry points (no exports): `main.ts` starts the API on `PORT` with `DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` and `BETTER_AUTH_URL` (it refuses to start without the last two, and on a database where the address tokens are issued for cannot be stored, as one that lacks its tables: `auth.started()`; the test clock under `QANDO_TEST_CLOCK=on`; under `QANDO_TEST_APPLICATIONS=on` the applications' documents are the example ones of `exampleApplications`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`, and none is read over the network: only the acceptance tests set either), and sends sign-in codes and the events' emails through the SMTP server of `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT` (587 by default), `SMTP_SECURE` (TLS required unless `false`, for a local sink), `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` and `MAIL_FROM` (`qando <no-reply@qando.app>` by default); without `SMTP_HOST` it warns and every delivery fails (`502` for a code); the events' emails go out from the outbox, which `main.ts` runs in the same process 30 seconds after each run has ended and stops on `SIGTERM` before the database pool is closed; what qando no longer keeps is deleted by `deleteExpired` (`apps/api/src/retention`) in the same process once an hour, each run logged with how many events, cancelled events and accounts it deleted, and stopped on `SIGTERM` as the outbox is (under `QANDO_TEST_CLOCK=on` it never runs: the real time would delete the scenarios' events); under `QANDO_TEST_CLOCK=on` it never runs on its own and `POST /api/test/send-due-emails` with `{ "to": [...] }` sends what is due at the request's time to those recipients instead (`204`; `400` without the list), so each acceptance scenario sends only its own emails; date phrases are copy-edited through Google's Gemini API with the key of `GEMINI_API_KEY` (paid tier), and without it `main.ts` warns and every phrase is read as written; `migrate.ts` applies the migrations before every deploy; `seed.ts` stores the demo events and prints their links; `delete-participant.ts` deletes one participant's vote on request (`npm run db:delete-participant`, `apps/api/src/retention`).

### `apps/api/src/db`

**Summary:** Database connection, schema, migrations and health probe.

**Purpose:** Everything that touches PostgreSQL directly besides the repositories. The schema guards what must never be stored whatever the code does: links that collide, a vote for another event's option, two preferred options, degenerate date or time ranges, an event without an owner (an account that owns events cannot be deleted), a second email of the same type for an event, an email recorded sent without the time it was sent (or with one while not sent), a second consent of one account for the same application. The account tables are Better Auth's core tables, with its columns and one of qando's (`users.last_seen_at`, when the account was last used), read and written only through `apps/api/src/modules/auth`. So are the tables of its token signing and of its OAuth provider, with which an account allows an application (an AI assistant) to act for it: every column is the library's, and what an account allowed (its consents, the tokens given for it, the applications registered under it) is deleted with the account by its foreign keys, as an application's consents, tokens and links to resources are with the application; a token outlives the session it was issued in.

### `apps/api/src/email`

**Summary:** The emails' shared frame and templates, sent over SMTP at once or queued with retries.

**Purpose:** The edge to the email server: the port every email goes through and its one implementation with Nodemailer, the same against Scaleway in production and a local SMTP sink in development and tests. And the outbox the emails of an event go through: queued in the `notifications` table in the same transaction as the change that calls for them, then sent one at a time, each failed attempt tried again after a longer wait (1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes) until the fifth, which records it failed. Every email is written in the shared frame (`renderEmail`) as blocks, which give both its HTML and its plain text, so the two always say the same; the templates of the event's emails, written when the outbox sends them, live here, and the sign-in code's in the module that sends it. Emails are Spanish only until the en catalogue exists, their dates named here as the results page names them.

### `apps/api/src/modules`

**Summary:** One folder per API resource.

**Purpose:** Each module is a router built from a port (its view of the database) and the clock; the repository behind the port lives in the same folder. Routers never touch the database directly, so their unit tests replace the port.

### `apps/api/src/modules/auth`

**Summary:** Sign-in by email code, sessions, the session request, sign-out, deleting an account with a code, the authorization server for applications and who may call the connector, through Better Auth.

**Purpose:** The only place that knows Better Auth: its Drizzle adapter on the account tables of `apps/api/src/db` and its email-code plugin, and its token signing, its OAuth provider and its reading of the document an application publishes about itself, with which an account allows an application (an AI assistant) to act for it: the authorization server, of which only a short list of routes is served (`authorizationServerOf`). Codes have 6 digits, are stored hashed, last 10 minutes and 5 wrong tries, and a new one replaces the last; the first code an email signs in with creates its account, already verified. Only sign-in codes are sent (qando has no passwords to reset); the code that deletes an account is one of them, in an email of its own, so an email keeps a single code with its tries and expiry. A session is the cookie `qando.session_token` (`__Secure-qando.session_token` over HTTPS): HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure over HTTPS, valid 90 days from its last use and renewed at most once a day. Better Auth's Origin check stays on in every environment (it skips it under `NODE_ENV=test` otherwise). None of Better Auth's own sign-in and session routes is served: qando's routes call it behind their own Origin checks (`sessionOriginCheck`, `ownPagesOnly`). Sign-out is ours because Better Auth's logs a failed deletion and still answers success; sending the code is ours so that a failed delivery reaches the page (`502`) and the email is qando's own, and signing in is ours so that a wrong code answers the tries left, which Better Auth keeps but does not answer. A sign-in made on the way to connecting an application (its page was opened by the request to connect) is answered where the browser goes on with that request. The tokens the authorization server gives are checked here too: who may call the connector, the address assistants call (`/api/mcp`, served by `apps/api/src/modules/connector`), is `connectorAccessOf`.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                                | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createAuth(dependencies)`, `Auth` (`auth.ts`)                                        | Better Auth over qando's database, under `/api/auth`. Its own code sending is never reached: its callback rejects. No request deletes the expired codes of others (`verification.disableCleanup`): the scheduled deletion deletes them, and a request only its own (the code it uses up, or finds expired). A session keeps neither the IP address nor the browser of the request that created it, whatever route that was; a session created or renewed (at most once a day) records its account's last use (`lastSeenAt`), and so does a token given to an application or renewed by it: using qando through an assistant is a use of the account. Every table of every plugin is given to the adapter (with one missing, Better Auth fails whatever it is asked). The OAuth provider sends a browser to the sign-in page (`/sign-in`) and to the consent page (`/connect`), and issues tokens for `<baseURL>/api/mcp`, the connector, the address assistants call, which it stores in `oauth_resources` when it starts and which must be HTTPS, or HTTP on this computer (`createAuth` throws otherwise). `started()` resolves once Better Auth has started with that address stored and fails if it is not: the API waits for it before it listens, so no request ever has to store it. `inTurn(turn, work)` is `wholeRequests`' work in a turn (`WholeRequests.inTurn`), in which `emailCodesOf` swaps and tries an email's code. An application may be allowed three things, asked for at once: to read the account's events (`events:read`), to create and manage them (`events:manage`) and to keep its access while the organizer is away (`offline_access`, without which no refresh token is issued); never `openid`, as qando is not an identity provider. It connects with a code and renews with a refresh token, the only two grants. An access token is signed, lasts 1 hour and is issued for the connector's address, and none is stored: a request to connect or for tokens that names nothing it asks access to (`resource`, or only an empty one, in the address of the first and in the form of the second) asks for the connector, the default the rules leave to the server, where Better Auth would give it a token for no address, which the connector refuses, and store it; so a refresh token given for no address, before that default, renews into the connector's tokens; a refresh token lasts 30 days from its last use, as each renewal replaces it and starts the 30 days again. An application is read from the document it publishes at its own address, which must say its name and where it returns to; applications cannot register themselves, and reading a session signs no token for the browser, so no signing key is created until a token is. A request to connect, for tokens or to hand one back dates every application it names (each `client_id` of its address and of its form, and the subject of each statement it signed; `updatedAt`) before Better Auth reads one, so the scheduled deletion (`deleteNoLongerKept`) never takes one a request is using. A token request (`POST /api/auth/oauth2/token`) is whole (`wholeRequests`) from the moment it reads its code or its refresh token: the refresh token or code it uses up, the tokens it gives and the use of the account are kept together or not at all, so a request that fails midway can be sent again and succeeds; a refusal keeps what it wrote (a refresh token used again after 30 seconds loses its whole family). Renewals of the same refresh token take turns (`inTurnsBy: 'token'`, the field Better Auth asks for it by): of two sent at once, the second waits for the first and is answered with the same tokens, where Better Auth alone refuses the one that loses with `invalid_grant`; codes are not taken in turns. An account keeps one consent per application: of two "Permitir" sent at once from two tabs, both find none and both create one, and the second is written over the first's (`consentsWrittenOver`), so both return to the application with a code, where Better Auth alone would store two consents. A refresh token is found only while the account allows its application, and a code only while the account allows it since the code was given (`onlyWhileConnected`): Better Auth alone looks at no consent when it exchanges a code or renews a token, so a renewal on its way while the account disconnects the application, or a code given before, would leave a token behind. The consent page's answer is not whole: Better Auth may read the application's document again and store it while answering it. An application that signs its requests (`private_key_jwt`, as ChatGPT does) presents with each a proof taken once, which Better Auth alone records as used while it identifies the application, so that a signed request that failed midway is refused when sent again; here the proof is held back (`heldBack`, the `oauthClientAssertion` model) and recorded when the request reads its code or its refresh token, with what the request gives: a signed request that failed midway can be sent again unchanged, one sent again after it was answered is refused with `invalid_client` as Better Auth refuses it, and a request refused before that read records its proof as it ends. A proof presented a second time refuses its request wherever it is found recorded, at that read or as the request ends without it, and whatever Better Auth answered (`refusal`). A request that hands a refresh token back (`POST /api/auth/oauth2/revoke`) is whole in the same way, from the moment it reads that token: the token marked as handed back and the proof of a signed request are kept together or not at all, so one that failed midway can be sent again unchanged, and it takes its turn with a renewal of the same token; a proof presented a second time is refused there too, with `invalid_client`, whatever the token is and whatever the request says it is. That route answers as its rules ask (RFC 7009), where Better Auth alone does not: the token is looked for as every kind the server knows, whatever the request says it is (`token_type_hint` is left out of what Better Auth reads), so a live refresh token said to be an access token is handed back all the same; and a token there is nothing to hand back of (one the server does not know, one handed back already, which costs the application every refresh token it holds for that account) is answered `200`, as done, where Better Auth answers `400` ("token not found"), the one answer of its that is turned into done. It still refuses an application that is not identified (`invalid_client`), a request that names no token (`invalid_request`) and an access token (`unsupported_token_type`), which is signed and of which nothing is stored to take back. What it stored before that read (an application's document, read again) is kept at once, whatever becomes of the request: Better Auth remembers in memory having stored it and would not store it again. The document and the keys an application publishes are read through `fetchApplicationDocument`, before which the request commits what it wrote and gives its connection back. A failure inside one of Better Auth's routes is thrown to the API (`onAPIError.throw`), which answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` and logs it as any other, never with the query that failed; on the route a refresh token is handed back at, Better Auth catches a failure of the database and answers a bare `500`, which `wholeRequests` turns back into that failure. |

Every other request goes on to the next handler, so none of Better Auth's other routes is served (registering an application, introspecting a token, its own sign-in and session routes), nor one an upgrade adds. `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/auth` answers the server's metadata as a document of ours: of Better Auth's, only what qando does, taken by name (not the address to introspect tokens, which it always announces and is not served, nor a logout qando has not, nor whatever an upgrade adds), with `none` and `private_key_jwt` as the ways an application says who it is to ask for tokens and to hand one back (an application's document may hold no shared secret), and the privacy page (`<baseURL>/privacy`) as its policy and its terms. A `HEAD` is served, counted and answered as the `GET` it stands for, without the body. A client address may send these routes, the metadata among them, 60 requests a minute, counted together past the hosting's proxies (`requestLimit` of `apps/api/src/http`) and refused past them with `429 RATE_LIMITED`; a request for anything else is neither counted nor refused here. This is the only limit on them: Better Auth's own is off (`createAuth`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

email), the cookie renewed while reading it (which Better Auth only returns to our routes), and ending a session: deleted first, so a failure rejects, then its cookies cleared.
