| `wholeRequests(db)`, `WholeRequests`, `Queries` (`whole-requests.ts`)                 | A database for Better Auth in which a request is whole from the moment it reaches what it gives or takes, used only by `createAuth`. `adapter(over, taken, heldBack?)` is what Better Auth is given as its `database` (`over` makes its drizzle adapter on the pool or on a request's transaction; `taken` lists the models a request gives or takes, each as `{ model, inTurnsBy? }`; `heldBack`, `{ model, storedAlready, refusal }`, names a model whose rows a request stores once on its way there; `findOne`, `findMany` and `count` are its reads, any other method writes). `asOne(handler)` is the handler with each request whole from its first call on one of the `taken` models, a read or a write: until then it is as any other request, each write kept as soon as it is made, a transaction of the library's too; from that call on, a read too, everything it does runs in one transaction on one connection, one call at a time, so what it reads of what it gives or takes, and a lock taken with that read, is held until it is over; each write is a savepoint, so one that fails undoes only itself and code that catches a refused write goes on as before; a transaction of the library's nests inside as a savepoint, and a call made from inside a write joins it instead of waiting for it. A model with `inTurnsBy` names the field its rows are asked for by: a request's call that names a value for that field takes its turn on that row first, as a write (its transaction opens there if none is open), and keeps the turn until the request is over, so of two requests that ask for the same row at once the second waits before it reads the row and reads what the first left; the turn is a lock PostgreSQL holds as long as the transaction (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`), ended with it however it ends; a call for another row, one that names no value for the field and one outside a request do not wait. A row of the `heldBack` model that a request creates before it is whole is not stored then: the call answers the row as it was given, and the row is stored as the request becomes whole, after the turn and in the same write as the call that made it whole, so it is kept or undone with the request. If the database refuses the row as stored already (a unique violation), that call fails with what `storedAlready()` makes, which stops the handler; while the row could not be stored, for that or another reason, every call of the request fails and is undone. A request answered while it still holds a row back stores it as it ends, each row in a write of its own, kept unless the answer is a fault; one that cannot be stored then for another reason fails the request. A request whose row was found stored already, as it became whole or as it ended, is refused: it is answered with what `refusal()` makes in place of whatever its handler answered, a fault too; a handler that fails still fails the request. Outside a request, and in one that is whole already, such a row is written as any other. The transaction is committed before the answer is returned, and undone when the answer is a `5xx` or the handler fails; a `4xx` keeps what was written; a commit that fails fails the request. A handler that answers a `5xx` after a call of the request failed has caught that failure: the request fails with what the last such call failed with, as if the handler had let it through. Once a request is over, what it still writes is refused if it was undone (a commit that failed undid it) and written through the pool once it is kept otherwise. `write(work)` is a write of our own: part of the request it is made in once that request is whole, made at once before that and outside one. `waiting(wait)` is a wait for another server: what the request wrote so far is committed first and its connection given back, its turn with it, so no connection is held through the wait; asked from inside a write it throws. `inTurn(turn, work)` is work of our own, whole and in its turn from its start, asked outside a request: one transaction on one connection that first waits for the turn named `turn` (the same lock, which every process over the database asks for) and holds it until the work is over; every call of the library, every `write` and every query on the `queries` it is given is part of it, kept when the work answers and undone when it fails, and a commit that fails fails the work; once it is over, what it still writes is refused if it was undone and written through the pool otherwise; `waiting` inside it throws. `Queries` is the pool or a request's transaction, as a query is sent to it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `consentsWrittenOver(factory)` (`consents-written-over.ts`) | Better Auth's database made by `factory`, in which creating an account's consent to an application it has a consent to already (the database keeps one per account and application, and refuses the second) writes the new answer over it, as Better Auth writes an answer over a consent it finds: its permissions, what it was given for and when it was answered. It answers the consent as then stored. Every other call and any other failure are the database's own. Two "Permitir" sent at once both find no consent and both create one: the second goes on as an allowance. |
| `deleteNoLongerKept(queries, now)` (`no-longer-kept.ts`) | Deletes, in the caller's transaction, the accounts that own no event and were last used (a session created or renewed, or a token given to an application or renewed by it) more than 6 months before `now`, by the calendar in UTC, with their sessions, what they allowed applications to do (consents and tokens, by their keys to the account) and what is left of the events they cancelled; the sessions and then the sign-in codes (which hold the email they were asked for, and also the proofs that a token is bound to a key) expired by `now`, in the order a code exchange takes them (`onlyWhileConnected`); and what applications were given that Better Auth can no longer take, so it answers every request as it would with the rows stored: the refresh tokens past their expiry (a replaced one stays until then, as presenting it again takes back the application's tokens), the access tokens stored past their expiry, the applications read from their document that no account allowed, that hold no token and that no request named for a day (`createAuth`'s handler dates every application a request names before the library reads one, so one in use is never deleted; connecting one again reads its document again), and the proofs of signed requests past their expiry. Answers how many accounts it deleted. |

**Depends on:** `apps/api/src/db`, `apps/api/src/email`, `apps/api/src/http`, `apps/api/src/modules/connector` (the `ConnectorAccess` port), `packages/contracts/src/auth` (also the connector's path, `connectorPath`), `packages/domain/src`.

**Used by:** `apps/api/src`, `apps/api/src/retention`.

### `apps/api/src/modules/connector`

**Summary:** The connector, a remote MCP server at `/api/mcp` that assistants call, and its tools.

**Purpose:** Serves `/api/mcp`, the connector: a remote MCP server (built with the protocol's TypeScript SDK), one more way into the API's use cases, for the applications (AI assistants) an account allowed to act for it. It answers the 2026-07-28 revision of the protocol and the 2025 ones, each request on its own: no conversation is kept between two, so a `GET` or a `DELETE`, which the 2025 revisions listen and hang up with, is answered `405`; a request with any other method is not one of the connector's and finds no route (`404`). An assistant of either reads the same presentation of qando when it connects (in the answer to `server/discover` or to `initialize`): its name and title, its website, the pages' public address, its symbol as an icon inline in the answer, as Claude takes one (a PNG or JPEG of 64 to 128 px under 10 kB; it fetches none from an address), and what it is told of qando (`instructions`), written in Spanish, the only language of this version; and is offered the same tools (`tools/list`). A tool is one thing an application can do for the account it acts for, with a use case of the API behind it; today there are eight, `read_date_phrase` ("Leer fechas de una frase"), the dates of a phrase as the wizard reads them (`InterpretPhrase`, `apps/api/src/modules/date-interpretations`), `create_event` ("Crear un evento"), an event created for the account as the wizard creates it, once however many times an assistant sends it within 10 minutes and at most 10 an hour (`createEventOnce`, `apps/api/src/modules/events`), `list_my_events` ("Ver mis eventos"), the account's events as "Mis eventos" lists them (`listMyEvents`, `apps/api/src/modules/management`), `read_event` ("Ver un evento"), one of them as its voting page shows it with its results as the results page shows them (`readOrganizerEvent`, `apps/api/src/modules/results`), and `confirm_option` ("Confirmar la fecha"), which changes what was there for good: the final date of one of the account's events, always in two calls, the first, without a code, changing nothing and answering what confirming would do, the notes of the web's question before confirming that apply and a code, the second, with that code, confirming (`confirmAsAsked`, `apps/api/src/modules/management`), `change_deadline` ("Cambiar el plazo") and `close_voting` ("Cerrar la votación"), the last day to vote and voting closed now, in one call each (`changeDeadline`, `closeVoting`), and `cancel_event` ("Cancelar un evento"), the event deleted for good, in two calls as confirming (`cancelEvent`). Every tool answers words, which the assistant reads, and beside them the same as data, which a view can draw, or, when it did not do what was asked (an event the web would refuse), words alone that say why, answered as not done; each says what a call does to what the account has: it only reads, and an assistant may call it without asking the organizer, or it adds and changes nothing already there, which it says, since the protocol takes a tool that does not say it only reads as one that may destroy, or it changes what was there for good, and is marked destructive. `serverFor` is the one place where a tool's answer becomes the protocol's, the same for every tool, so a new tool says only its name, its title and description, its effect, the shape of what it takes and of its data, and what it answers. The list of tools is the same until the next deployment and says so: no application needs to listen for changes. An account may call tools 60 times in any minute, on the clock the API is given (`quota`, `apps/api/src/http`); a call past that is not run and is answered in words with the time to wait, since an assistant reads a tool's answer, not a status, and asking what the connector offers is not counted. A call to a tool that fails is logged and answered in fixed words, as the failure's own message may name what is stored. Text a person wrote (a title, a note, a name) goes between « » in every answer (`written`), the mark the presentation tells the assistant to read as data, never as instructions. A request sent by a page of another site is refused `403 FORBIDDEN` before its token is looked at (`noForeignPages`, `apps/api/src/http`); one without `Origin` is an assistant's own server calling and goes on to the access check. Who may call is a port, `ConnectorAccess`, which `apps/api/src/modules/auth` implements over Better Auth (`connectorAccessOf`): this folder knows nothing of tokens, takes from the check who calls (`Caller`): the account a request acts for and the connected application, and answers what the check answers to a request it refuses, its status, headers and body. A body over 32 kB is refused `413`: creating an event, the largest call an assistant makes, sends up to 16 kB on the web. No answer is cached, an event stream's neither: the mark the protocol's handler gives a stream is replaced by `no-store, no-transform`. A failure while serving a request, of the access check or of the protocol's handler, is logged as every failed request of the API is and answered `500` in the protocol's own shape, without a word of what failed; a request the protocol refuses is an answer and logs nothing. The address a request arrived at is never read: its `Host` may say anything.

**Exports:**

| Export | What it does |
| ------ | ------------ |
| `connectorRouter(access, sessions, { managedEvents, interpret, newEvents, eventResults }, { now, website, logError, confirmationSecret })` (`connector.ts`) | The router of `/api/mcp` for `POST`, `GET` and `DELETE` (any other method goes on to the rest of the API, which has no route for it): `noStore`, `noForeignPages` (`403`), then the request, with its method and its headers (where the token is), is served by `access` around the MCP handler, and what that answers is sent as it is: the check's refusal, or the handler's answer. The handler answers each request with the server of the caller `access` says its token is of (`serverFor`): it names itself `qando`, titled `qando`, version `1.0.0`, with `website` as its website and `icon` as its icon, presents qando with `texts.server.instructions`, offers the tools (`readDatesTool`, over `interpret`, then `createEventTool`, over `newEvents`, the port of `apps/api/src/modules/events`, `now` and `website`, then `listEventsTool`, over `managedEvents`, the port of `apps/api/src/modules/management`, and `now`, then `readEventTool`, over `managedEvents`, `eventResults`, the port of `apps/api/src/modules/results`, `now` and `website`, then `confirmOptionTool`, over `managedEvents`, the codes `confirmationCodes(confirmationSecret)` makes and `now`, then `changeDeadlineTool` and `closeVotingTool`, over `managedEvents` and `now`, then `cancelEventTool`, over `managedEvents`, the same codes and `now`) and keeps nothing between two requests (`GET` and `DELETE` answer `405` with `Allow: POST`; a request to listen is answered at once that there is nothing to listen for, and ended: no stream is held open). One count holds every account's calls to tools, 60 in any minute each, on `now`. An answer sent as an event stream goes out `no-store, no-transform`. A body over 32 kB answers `413`. A failure of the check, or what the handler reported before it answered `500`, goes to `logError` as `Request failed` with the method, the route and `describeError` of the error (`apps/api/src/http`), and is answered `500`; a call to a tool that fails is logged the same way and answered as a tool answers; what the handler reports of a request it refuses is not logged. |
| `ConnectorAccess` (`connector.ts`) | The port, who may call the connector: given how the connector serves a request for an account (`ServedFor`), how it serves one once the caller is known (`Served`). A request that carries no access token issued for the connector, or one whose application is no longer connected to the account, is answered by the check itself, with the `401` that says where to ask for access; any other reaches the connector as it came, with the account its token is of and its application (a `Caller`). |
| `Served` (`connector.ts`) | How a request is answered, in the web's own `Request` and `Response`: `(calling: Request) => Promise<Response>`. |
| `ServedFor` (`connector.ts`) | How the connector answers the request of an application that acts for an account: `(calling: Request, caller: Caller) => Promise<Response>`, the account its token is of and its application. |
| `serverFor(caller, serving)`, `Serving` (`tool.ts`) | The MCP server that answers one request of an application acting for the account: qando's presentation (its name and title, `website`, `icon` and `texts.server.instructions`) and the tools of `serving` (a `Serving`: the `tools`; `calls`, each account's calls (counted by `caller.accountId`), a `Quota` of `apps/api/src/http`; `failed`, told of a call that failed, to log it; and `website`, qando's website, the pages' public address). It says that its list of tools never changes. The one place where a tool's answer becomes the protocol's, the same for every tool: its words as text and its data beside them as structured content, checked against the shape the tool announces before it leaves; a `Refused` answered in its words alone, as not done; each tool is registered with its input shape and with what its effect tells an application (one that only reads, that it only reads; one that adds, that it neither only reads nor destroys; one that changes, that it is destructive), so a call whose arguments do not fit is answered by the protocol's library, in words saying what does not fit, before it is counted or run; a call `calls` refuses is not run and is answered in words with the time to wait (`texts.limits.calls`), and only calls to a tool count; a call that fails, also one whose data does not fit the shape, is told to `failed` and answered in fixed words (`texts.answers.failed`), never the failure's own message, which may name what is stored. Both are answered as what a tool did not do, not as a failure of the protocol. |
| `icon` (`icon.ts`) | qando's symbol as the connector shows it, the `Icon` of its presentation: the picture of the site's `favicon.ico` scaled to 96 px, a PNG of under 4 kB written inline as a `data:` address (`image/png`, `96x96`), as Claude takes one: a PNG or JPEG of 64 to 128 px under 10 kB, never fetched from an address, in a presentation of under about 16,000 characters. Changing the site's symbol means making it again. |
| `Tool`, `Said` (`tool.ts`) | One thing an application can do through the connector for the account it acts for (`Tool<Input, Data>`): the `name` applications call it by, the `title` the organizer sees in the chat, the `description` the assistant reads to know when to call it, `effect` (an `Effect`: what a call does to what the account has), `input` (the shape of what a call gives it, a Zod schema; an empty object when it takes nothing), `data` (the shape of the data beside its words, a Zod schema) and `answer(caller, input)`, what it answers the caller from a use case of the API: a `Said<Data>`, its `text` and its `data`, or a `Refused` when it did not do what was asked. |
| `Effect` (`tool.ts`) | What a call does to what the account has: `'reads'`, it only reads it, so an assistant may call the tool without asking the organizer; `'adds'`, it adds to it and changes nothing already there; `'changes'`, it changes what was there for good, which `serverFor` says is destructive. The protocol takes a tool that does not say it only reads as one that may destroy, so `serverFor` says of one that adds that it does not. |
| `Caller` (`tool.ts`) | Who a call is from: `accountId`, the account the application acts for, and `applicationId`, the connected application as its access token names it. |
| `Refused` (`tool.ts`) | A tool's answer when what was asked was not done: `{ refused }`, words alone that say why, which `serverFor` answers as not done, with no data. |
| `readDatesTool(interpret)` (`read-dates.ts`) | "Leer fechas de una frase", the tool `read_date_phrase`, which only reads: it takes `phrase` (1 to 120 characters once trimmed, the wizard's limit) and `timeZone` (an IANA name) and answers the same reading as the wizard's (`InterpretPhrase` of `apps/api/src/modules/date-interpretations`, with `copyEdit: false`: the assistant writes the phrase), read in that time zone, as an event can hold it (`heldReading`): the options, the questions to ask first and the notices, in words and as data (the contract's `DateInterpretation` shape), with each time range left out and each question not asked, and why and what to use instead: each range once, with its days, both readings of a question not asked among them, in the order of the calendar (by first day, then by time). Its words are in `texts.reading`. |
| `createEventTool(newEvents, now, website)` (`create-event.ts`) | "Crear un evento", the tool `create_event`, which adds: it takes the event as the wizard sends it, the contract's `title`, `note`, `options` (each option's shape written out whole, so an application has no definition to follow), `deadline` and `timeZone`, with `organizerName` and `anonymous` that may be left out (voting with names then), and creates it for the account through `createEventOnce` (`apps/api/src/modules/events`) at the time `now` answers: the same event sent again within 10 minutes is the first one, and an account creates at most 10 events an hour. It answers the voting link alone, built on `website` by `votingLinkOf`, never the results link nor the management link, which reaches the organizer only in the summary email: in words, "Evento creado:" with the title between « », the link to share and that the summary was emailed (`texts.answers.created`), and as data `{ id, title, votingLink }`, `id` being the identifier the other tools take the event by. An event the web would refuse is not created: a `Refused` with a first line and each problem on its own line (`texts.answers.notCreated`), in the order `validateNewEvent` lists them, each said once however many options have it, an option's problem naming its day (days by their first day) and, for a time off the quarters, the time that is (`onQuarter`, `packages/domain/src`), and nothing then of the time range within a single clock hour of an option that starts off the quarters, whose way to the next hour would be off them too; a range of days that ends before it starts is told so, apart from one of a single day. An account past its 10 events of the hour is refused with the wait (`texts.limits.events`). |
| `listEventsTool(managedEvents, now)` (`list-events.ts`) | "Ver mis eventos", the tool `list_my_events`, which only reads: the account's events as `listMyEvents` (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) answers them, newest first, each in its state at the time `now` answers. Its words are a line over the list ("Tienes 3 eventos:") and one line per event: the title between « », the state ("Votación abierta hasta el 1 de julio de 2026", "Votación cerrada el…", "Fecha confirmada"), how many people have voted and the identifier of its voting link, by which the other tools take an event; an account that has none is answered "Aún no has creado ningún evento.". The data beside the words is `{ events }`, the same list as `GET /api/me/events` answers (`MyEvent`, `packages/contracts/src/management`), its shape written out whole, so an application has no definition to follow. |
| `readEventTool(managedEvents, eventResults, now, website)` (`read-event.ts`) | "Ver un evento", the tool `read_event`, which only reads: it takes `id`, the identifier of an event's voting link that `listEventsTool` answers, and answers the event as `readOrganizerEvent` (`apps/api/src/modules/results`) reads it for the account at the time `now` answers. Its words, a line each: the title between « », its state and how many people have voted, as a line of the list says them; "Enlace para votar:" with the voting link built on `website` by `votingLinkOf`, never the results link nor the management link; the note between « »; "Voto anónimo: los resultados no tienen nombres." on an anonymous event; "Opciones:" ("Opciones (hora de Madrid):" when an option has a time, the city of the event's time zone) and one line per option; the confirmed date; then, once someone has voted, the results in the words of the results page: the count of the votes, provisional or final, the sentence of their outcome ("La fecha elegida es:", "Hay un empate entre dos opciones:"…), each date that wins and each alternative ("Fecha alternativa:") with how many answered it each way ("Preferida", "Disponible", "No puede"), each count with the names of who did between « » unless the event is anonymous. Another account's event and one that does not exist are answered alike, "No hay ningún evento tuyo con ese identificador.", and a cancelled one with its title, each as not done. The data beside the words is `{ id, votingLink, event, results }`: the event as `GET /api/public/events/:id` answers it (`PublicEvent`, `packages/contracts/src/public-events`) and its results as `GET /api/results/:resultsId` does (`Results`, `packages/contracts/src/results`), their shapes written out whole with the contract's descriptions, so an application has no definition to follow. |
| `confirmOptionTool(managedEvents, codes, now)` (`confirm-option.ts`) | "Confirmar la fecha", the tool `confirm_option`, which changes: it takes `{ id, option: { dates, time }, code? }`, the event's identifier and the date named by its days and time as "Ver un evento" gives them, matched against the event's options as the same date (`sameOption`, `packages/domain/src`). Called without a code it changes nothing and answers, a line each: that nothing is confirmed yet (or, when a code was sent that does not hold, that the date was not confirmed), the question, the notes of the web's question before confirming that apply (`confirmationNotes`, `packages/domain/src`: nobody voted, nobody can attend, not a date the results recommend with those it recommends, voting still open), that the confirmation is final, and the code with its 10 minutes (`codes.give`). Called again with that code it confirms through `confirmAsAsked` (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) and says the date is confirmed and voting closed. A code that does not hold (expired, for another date or another application, never given, or the facts changed: a vote, the recommended dates, voting closed, also when they change while the event is locked, when the event is read again) confirms nothing and is answered as a new first answer with a new code. Refused: a date confirmed already, with that date; a date that is no option; another organizer's event, as one that does not exist; a cancelled one. Data: `{ id, option, confirmed, code }`. |
| `confirmationCodes(secret)`, `ConfirmationCodes`, `Asked`, `Confirming`, `Cancelling` (`confirmation-code.ts`) | The codes of the connector's confirmations, which stand for the organizer's yes, stored nowhere: `give(asked, at)` and `holds(code, asked, at)`, for what the organizer is asked (`Asked`): a `Confirming` (`action: 'confirm'`, the account, application, event, option and the `DecisionFacts`, `packages/domain/src`, the notes were said from) or a `Cancelling` (`action: 'cancel'`, the account, application and event). A code is a 40-bit HMAC-SHA256 signature, under a key derived from `secret` (HKDF), of those with the action first (the facts as `factsWritten` writes them) and the second it was given in, so a code given to confirm never cancels nor the other way round, written as 8 of Crockford's letters and digits in two groups of four ("K7P2-9QMX"); it holds during the 10 minutes after, read whatever its case, with or without its hyphen and the spaces around it. |
| `changeDeadlineTool(managedEvents, now)` (`change-deadline.ts`) | "Cambiar el plazo", the tool `change_deadline`, which changes: it takes `{ id, deadline }`, the event's identifier and the new last day to vote (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the contract's), in one call, as it can be changed again, and changes it through `changeDeadline` (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) as the management page does: any day from today to 12 months ahead in the event's time zone, earlier than the current one too. It answers "Plazo cambiado:" with the title between « » and the new day, or "Votación reabierta:" when voting was closed. Refused: a day passed or more than 12 months ahead, each in words; a date confirmed, with that date, also when it is confirmed while the deadline changes; another organizer's event, as one that does not exist; a cancelled one. Data: `{ id, state: 'open', deadline }` (`votingSchema`). |
| `closeVotingTool(managedEvents, now)`, `votingSchema` (`close-voting.ts`) | "Cerrar la votación", the tool `close_voting`, which changes: it takes `{ id }` and closes voting now through `closeVoting` (`apps/api/src/modules/management`), in one call, as a new deadline reopens it: "Votación cerrada:" with the title between « », that the results go by email and how to reopen it. Voting closed before the call (by its deadline, or a call before) changes nothing and is answered with the day it closed. Refused: a date confirmed, with that date, also when it is confirmed while voting closes; another organizer's event, as one that does not exist; a cancelled one. `votingSchema` is the data of this tool and of `changeDeadlineTool`: `{ id, state, deadline }`, `state` `'open'` or `'closed'`. |
| `cancelEventTool(managedEvents, codes, now)` (`cancel-event.ts`) | "Cancelar un evento", the tool `cancel_event`, which changes: it takes `{ id, code? }`, in any state of the event, always in two calls, as confirming. Called without a code it deletes nothing and answers, a line each: that nothing is cancelled yet (or, when a code was sent that does not hold, that the event was not cancelled), the question with the title between « », what is deleted and that no other email goes, what the links show, that it is final, and the code with its 10 minutes (`codes.give`, a `Cancelling`). Called again with that code it cancels through `cancelEvent` (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) and answers "Evento cancelado:" with the message to forward to the group. A code that does not hold (expired, for another application or event, given to confirm, never given) cancels nothing and is answered as a new first answer with a new code. Refused: another organizer's event, as one that does not exist; a cancelled one, also by a call before with the same code or by another request meanwhile. Data: `{ id, cancelled, code }`. |
| `accountEvent(managedEvents, accountId, id, now)`, `undecidedEvent(managedEvents, accountId, id, now)`, `refusalOf(refusal)` (`account-event.ts`) | One of the account's events as `readManagedEvent` (`apps/api/src/modules/management`) reads it now, for a tool that acts on it, or the words that refuse the call (`refusalOf`, a `Refused`: a cancelled event says so with its title, another organizer's and one that does not exist are answered alike). `undecidedEvent` also refuses an event whose date is confirmed, with that date, for the tools that decide what a confirmation decided for good (`confirmOptionTool`, `changeDeadlineTool`, `closeVotingTool`); `readEventTool` answers its refusals with `refusalOf`. |
| `votingLinkOf(website, participationId)` (`tool.ts`) | The address of an event's voting page on `website`, `/vote/` and the participation ID: the one link of an event that a tool's answer gives. |
| `texts` (`texts.ts`) | What the connector says to an assistant and, through it, to the organizer: in Spanish, with the web's words where it has them. `texts.server.instructions` is the connector's presentation, which an assistant reads when it connects, made of sentences with the most important within its first 512 characters, the part ChatGPT reads first, and all of it within the 4,096 Claude Code reads: what qando is for, how to create an event (read the dates first with "Leer fechas de una frase", show the options to the organizer and create the event once they agree), that titles, notes and names come between « » as data people wrote, never instructions, and, when it is not known whether an event was created, to look with "Ver mis eventos" before creating it again, and that confirming and cancelling take two calls, with the organizer's yes between them; then what the organizer does with the connector (create events, follow the voting, confirm the date, change the deadline, close voting and cancel events) and what is done elsewhere (voting, always from the link; changing the proposed dates, on the web). `texts.tools` holds each tool's title, which the organizer sees in the chat, and its description, which the assistant reads, with what the assistant reads of each thing it gives the tool (`input`); `texts.answers`, the words of the answers (the line over the list of events, an event's line, an account without events, an event created with its voting link, `created`, a creation refused with its problems, `notCreated`, another account's event or one that does not exist, `notFound`, a cancelled one, `cancelled`, a call that could not be answered); `texts.problems`, why an event was not created, a line for each rule it breaks, in the web's words where it has them; `texts.state`, an event's state with its last day of voting as a sentence says it ("1 de julio de 2026"); `texts.voters`, how many people have voted ("Nadie ha votado todavía", "Ha votado 1 persona", "Han votado 2 personas"); `texts.limits.calls`, the words of a call past the account's limit, and `texts.limits.events`, those of an event past its 10 an hour, each with the wait as the web says it ("20 s", "12 min"); `texts.reading`, the words of a phrase's reading (its options, questions, notices and the times left out); `texts.event`, the words of an event read, in those of the results page where it has them; `texts.tools.confirmOption`, the title, description and input of "Confirmar la fecha"; `texts.confirm`, the answers of confirming (the first line, the line of a code that no longer holds, the question, the notes in the web's words without their bold, that it is final, the code's line, done, already confirmed, not an option); `texts.tools.changeDeadline`, `texts.tools.closeVoting` and `texts.tools.cancelEvent`, the title, description and input of each; `texts.cancel`, the answers of cancelling (the first line, the line of a code that does not hold, the question, what is deleted, what the links show, that it is final, the code's line, done with the message to forward); `texts.close`, those of closing voting (closed now, closed before with its day); `texts.deadline`, those of changing the deadline (changed, reopened, a day passed, more than 12 months ahead). An option is said the same in every answer: its days and its time, "sin horario" for a day without one ("viernes 19 de junio, sin horario"). |
| `written(text)` (`texts.ts`) | Text written by a person (a title, a note, a name) as every answer's words carry it: between « », the mark the connector's presentation tells the assistant to read as data, never as instructions. A « or » the person typed becomes “ or ”, so nothing typed closes the mark, and a line break or another control character one space, so nothing typed starts a line of its own; the data beside the words keeps the text as typed. |

**Depends on:** `apps/api/src/email`, `apps/api/src/http`, `apps/api/src/modules/date-interpretations`, `apps/api/src/modules/events`, `apps/api/src/modules/management`, `apps/api/src/modules/results`, `packages/contracts/src`, `packages/contracts/src/auth` (the connector's path, `connectorPath`), `packages/contracts/src/management`, `packages/date-reader`, `packages/domain/src`.

### `apps/api/src/modules/date-interpretations`

**Summary:** Read the dates and times a phrase says.

**Purpose:** Serves `POST /api/date-interpretations`: the dates and times a phrase in plain language says, for the page that creates an event to mark. The two parts that interpret a date phrase meet in `phraseInterpreter`, which knows nothing of HTTP, so another way in, the connector's tool `read_date_phrase` (`apps/api/src/modules/connector`), calls it with `copyEdit: false` and leaves the copy edit out: the phrase is copy-edited (`EditPhrase` of `apps/api/src/phrase-editor`, which answers it as written when the model is slow, fails or changes what it says) and then read by the rules reader (`readDates` of `packages/date-reader`), with today and the time now taken in the request's time zone. Every phrase gets an answer: what is not understood comes as notices, never as an error. Only qando's own pages are answered (`403 FORBIDDEN` otherwise), 20 times in any hour per client address (`429 RATE_LIMITED`), counted before anything is read, so a refusal never reaches the model; a body above 2 kB is refused unread (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`). The phrase is neither stored nor logged, and no answer is cached. The module has no port: it reads no database.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dateInterpretationsRouter(interpret, sessions)` (`date-interpretations.ts`)                         | The router of `POST /api/date-interpretations`: `noStore`, `ownPagesOnly` (`403`), `rollingHourLimit` of 20 in any hour per address (`429`), the body read against the contract (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`), then `interpret` of the body's phrase, time zone and region, with the copy edit; answers `200 { options, questions, notices }`.                                                                                                  |
| `phraseInterpreter(editPhrase, now)`, `InterpretPhrase`, `PhraseToInterpret` (`interpret-phrase.ts`) | The interpreter of date phrases, apart from HTTP: `InterpretPhrase` takes `{ text, timeZone, region?, copyEdit }` and answers the reading of `readDates` as an event can hold it (`heldReading`), as data. With `copyEdit` the phrase is first copy-edited by `editPhrase`; without it the phrase is read as given and the language model is not asked (a caller whose phrase is already well written). `today` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `now` (HH:MM) are those of the clock in `timeZone`. |
| `heldReading(reading)` (`held-reading.ts`) | What an event can hold of a reading, decided once for every client (the wizard and the connector): a time range an event cannot hold (within one clock hour, `withinOneHour` of `packages/domain/src`, or ending on the next day) is left out of its day, which is marked as a whole day unless another option gives it a time, and told once with its days (`timesLeftOut`). A question is asked when an event can hold one reading at least, saying the one it cannot (`leftOut`), which the organizer may still mean; when neither, nothing is asked and the question is told as read (`questionsNotAsked`). The questions still asked are numbered again; a day is a whole day or its times, marked once. |

**Depends on:** `apps/api/src/http`, `apps/api/src/phrase-editor` (the type `EditPhrase`), `packages/contracts/src/date-interpretations`, `packages/date-reader`, `packages/domain/src`.

**Used by:** `apps/api/src`, `apps/api/src/modules/connector`.

### `apps/api/src/modules/events`

**Summary:** Create an event: the use cases, the web's and an assistant's, and the web's route.

**Purpose:** Creates an event, through use cases free of HTTP so that every client runs the same checks: `createEvent`, behind `POST /api/events`, which this folder serves, and `createEventOnce`, behind the connector's tool `create_event` (`apps/api/src/modules/connector`). On the web, only a session creates: none, or an ended one, answers `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` before the body is read, and the session cookie from a page of another site or without `Origin` `403 FORBIDDEN`. The body is checked by `validateNewEvent` (`packages/domain/src`) with today in the event's time zone; every problem is answered at once (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`). The event is owned by the session's account, which keeps its email; the management token comes from the page in `X-Management-Token` and only its hash is stored; a send that repeats the token of an event of the same account stores nothing and answers that event again, and another account's token is refused (`MANAGEMENT_TOKEN_TAKEN`). Body limit 16 kB, never cached. The first event of a browser signs in through `apps/api/src/modules/auth` first. An assistant sends no token of its own: the token is made where the event is stored and answered to no one, so its owner manages the event with the session; a call that repeats the same event, the same in everything it holds, within 10 minutes (the assistant did not know whether its first one arrived) stores nothing and answers that event, and an account that created 10 events in the last hour, whatever created them, creates none from an assistant until the first of them leaves the hour; a name the assistant leaves out is the organizer name of the account's last event, as the web proposes it (`GET /api/me/organizer-name`, which this folder serves too: `401` without a session, never cached). Every event is stamped with its creation time on the clock the API is given, which these counts are taken on.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createEvent(newEvents, ownerId, managementToken, input, now)`, `EventCreation` (`create-event.ts`) | The use case, free of HTTP: checks the event with today taken from `now` in its time zone (`validateNewEvent`) and stores it for its owner with the token given; answers `created` with its links, or `rejected` with every rule it breaks, or alone `MANAGEMENT_TOKEN_TAKEN`. |
| `createEventOnce(newEvents, ownerId, input, now)`, `AssistantEventInput`, `OnceCreation` (`create-event.ts`) | The use case behind creating an event from an assistant, free of HTTP, which sends no token: the event (an `AssistantEventInput`, whose `organizerName` may be left out) is checked as `createEvent` checks it, a name left out or only spaces being the organizer name of the account's last event (none without an event: the name is missing), and stored once (`createOnce`) under the assistant's rules, the same event within 10 minutes and at most 10 an hour; answers `created` with its title and links (also those of the same event created by a call before), `rejected` with every rule of the domain it breaks, or `limited` with the whole seconds to wait (`retryAfterSeconds`, at least 1). |
| `NewEvents`, `OnceRules` (`create-event.ts`) | The port: `create(ownerId, managementToken, event)` stores a valid new event for its owner and answers its IDs; the IDs of the event the token already holds when the owner's (nothing stored), `taken` when another account's. `createOnce(ownerId, event, rules)` stores it the same way for a client that sends no token, the token made there and answered to no one, with the account locked so two calls at once wait for each other: an event of the account the same in everything it holds (title, deadline, time zone, voting with or without names, note, organizer name and options), created less than `rules.sameWithinMs` ago, is the same event, so nothing is stored and its links are answered; an account that created `rules.atMost.count` events less than `rules.atMost.withinMs` ago, whatever created them, stores nothing and is answered when the next one can be (`{ retryAt }`). `lastOrganizerName(ownerId)` answers the organizer name of the account's most recently created event, none without one. |
| `createEventRouter(newEvents, sessions, now)` (`events.ts`) | The HTTP side: the session, the token header and the body, then `createEvent`: `201 { participationId, resultsId }` or `400` with its problems. Also `GET /api/me/organizer-name`: the session (`401` without one), then `lastOrganizerName` for its account: `200 { organizerName }`, `null` without an event. |
| `createNewEvents(db, now)` (`new-events-repository.ts`)           | The PostgreSQL implementation, one transaction per event: the owner's account locked and named after the organizer if it has no name yet, the event with two new links, the token's hash (an insert that meets the hash stores nothing and answers the event that holds it) and its creation time, read once from `now`, its summary email queued to the account's email, due at that time, and "voting closed", due once voting closes, and its options with their position in the order the domain gave. `createOnce` compares the options in that order and counts the account's events by their creation time. |

**Depends on:** `apps/api/src/db`, `apps/api/src/email`, `apps/api/src/http`, `apps/api/src/capability-token.ts`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`, `packages/contracts/src/management`, `packages/domain/src`.

**Used by:** `apps/api/src`, `apps/api/src/modules/connector`, `apps/api/src/test`.

### `apps/api/src/modules/management`

**Summary:** Manage an event with its management token or its owner's session; list the owner's events.

**Purpose:** Serves the management endpoints under `/api/events/:id`, `:id` being the participation ID of the link; `GET`, the event as its organizer manages it, `POST …/confirmation`, confirming its final option, `PUT …/options`, replacing every option while voting is open and nobody has voted, and `POST …/emails/:type/retry`, trying a failed email once more. Also "Mis eventos", `GET /api/me/events`: the events of the session's account, newest first, each in its current state and with how many people have voted (`401` without a session; a cancelled event is no longer listed, its remains have no owner); the use case behind it, `listMyEvents`, also answers the connector's tool `list_my_events` (`apps/api/src/modules/connector`). Who is acting is resolved in one place, `actingOrganizer`: every management use case calls it first and only gets on with an `ActingOrganizer`, which only that function makes, so the owner's session is one more way to resolve it (later an agent's grant too) without changing any use case; either credential that manages the event grants it. No credential answers `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` (a session that ended counts as none), credentials that do not manage the event (another event's token, any other link, the session of another account, an unknown event) `403 FORBIDDEN`, a cancelled event `410 EVENT_CANCELLED` with its title. The token travels in `X-Management-Token`, is matched by its hash and never logged; the session's account comes from `signedInAccount` (`apps/api/src/http`).

The event as it is now; an event cancelled by another request since the check answers `cancelled` (`changeManagedEvent`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `managementRouter(managedEvents, now)` (`management.ts`)                                                                                      | The HTTP side: reads the path, the token header, the signed-in account and the body (`400` names each broken part, never its value), answers each outcome with its status (`not-failed` as `409 EMAIL_NOT_FAILED`, `deleted` as `200 { title }`), never cached.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `listMyEvents(managedEvents, accountId, now)` (`list-my-events.ts`)                                                                           | The use case behind "Mis eventos", free of HTTP, so the API's route and the connector's tool `list_my_events` (`apps/api/src/modules/connector`) list the same: the account's events, newest first, each with its current state (`currentState`) and how many people have voted (`voters`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `myEventsRouter(managedEvents, sessions, now)` (`my-events.ts`)                                                                               | The HTTP side of `GET /api/me/events`: the session (`401` without one, before anything is read), the list as the contract shows it, never cached.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `createManagedEvents(db)` (`managed-events-repository.ts`)                                                                                    | The PostgreSQL implementation: the token matched by its hash and the session by the event's owner, in the query; the account's events by its owner index, newest first, their voters counted in the same query; only a refusal costs the read that tells a cancelled event apart. A change locks the event row `FOR UPDATE`, which waits for the votes holding it `FOR SHARE`. The event's emails are read the summary first; a confirmation drops the "voting closed" not sent (`dropUnsentVotingClosed`); a retry goes through `retryFailedEmail` (`apps/api/src/email`), the contract's `voting-closed` stored as `voting_closed`. Cancelling deletes the event row (waiting, like a change, for the votes being stored and for an email being sent; its options, votes, confirmation and emails cascade) and writes its `cancelled_events` row (participation ID, results ID, title, instant) in the same transaction. |

**Purpose:** Serves the voting page's sends and reads under `/api/public/events/:id/participations`: cast a vote (`POST`), read the vote of a token (`GET …/mine`) and replace it (`PUT …/mine`). | `StoredVotingEvent`, `VotingEventLookup`, `StoredParticipation` (`participations.ts`) | What the port answers: the event found, cancelled or missing; a stored participation.                                                                                                                              |
| `createParticipations(db)` (`participations-repository.ts`)                           | The PostgreSQL implementation of the port.                                                                                                                                                                         |

### `apps/api/src/modules/results`

**Summary:** Read the results by the results link.

**Purpose:** Serves `GET /api/results/:resultsId`: the domain's results (`resultsOf`) with each shown option in full and, on named events, the names of who answered it each way in Spanish alphabetical order (a name repeated by a later vote reads "Ana (2)"); final once voting is no longer open (`currentState`). ### `apps/api/src/phrase-editor`

**Summary:** The copy edit of a date phrase by a language model, and its limits.

**Purpose:** The first of the two parts that interpret a date phrase: before the rules reader reads it, a language model rewrites the phrase into a well-written one in the same language, so that "el vienres alas 9" is read as "el viernes a las 9". The model never reads dates and is never trusted. This folder is the edge to it and everything that keeps it harmless: the port the model sits behind, its one implementation with Google's Gemini API, the 3-second limit and the check of its answer in code (`keepsWhen` of `packages/date-reader`). Whatever goes wrong, the phrase is read as written: the editor never causes an error. A phrase is the organizer's text: it travels to the model as data, apart from the instructions, and is never logged, nor is the edit or an error, which may quote them.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `phraseEditor(copyEdit, log)`, `EditPhrase` (`phrase-editor.ts`) | **What the API uses.** `EditPhrase` answers the phrase the rules reader reads for a phrase as written, and always resolves. It asks the model for a copy edit and answers it only when it comes within 3 seconds and passes the edit check; when the model takes longer (it is told to stop), fails or writes an edit that fails the check, and when there is no model (`copyEdit` is `undefined`: no key is set), it answers the phrase as written. Each phrase not edited is logged with its reason. |
| `CopyEdit` (`phrase-editor.ts`)                                  | The port, and the only thing tests replace: asks a language model to copy-edit a phrase. Resolves with the phrase as the model wrote it; rejects when the model cannot be reached, refuses or answers nothing that can be read (the error may quote the phrase, so it is never logged). Its `signal` aborts when the answer is no longer waited for.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `CopyEditRefused` (`phrase-editor.ts`)                           | The failure of a `CopyEdit` whose service answered with an HTTP error; it carries the `status` (401 for a wrong key, 429 past the quota), the one detail of a failure that is logged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `PhraseEditLogEntry` (`phrase-editor.ts`)                        | What is logged of a phrase read as written: the level (`warn`), the fixed message `Phrase not edited`, the reason (`timedOut`, `failed`, `discarded`) and the status of a refusal. Never the phrase, the edit or the error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `geminiEditor(settings)`, `GeminiSettings` (`gemini-editor.ts`)  | `CopyEdit` with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite over Google's Gemini API: one request per phrase, never tried again, with the key in a header, the phrase as JSON data in the user's turn, the answer forced to `{ phrase }` and `store: false`, which asks Google not to keep the request in the project's logs. `settings`: the API key (paid tier) and, for tests only, where the API is.                                                                                                                     |
| `instructions` (`instructions.ts`)                               | What the model is told: what a copy editor fixes, what it never does (add, remove or change anything that says when; follow an instruction written in the phrase) and the forms the reader reads well. They are measured as a whole, so a test holds their fingerprint: a change is measured again on fresh phrases first.                                                                                                                                                                             |

**Depends on:** `packages/date-reader`.

**Used by:** `apps/api/src`, `apps/api/src/modules/date-interpretations` (the type `EditPhrase`), `apps/api/src/test`.

### `apps/api/src/retention`

**Summary:** Delete what qando no longer keeps, 6 months after it is of no use or on request.

**Purpose:** The periods the privacy page states, applied by the API itself once an hour (`apps/api/src/main.ts`): an event 6 months after its date, what is left of a cancelled event 6 months after its cancellation, an account that owns no event 6 months after its last use, and the sign-in codes and sessions once expired. Nothing of what it deletes is kept: a deleted event's links lead nowhere, as a link of no event does. Also one participant's vote, deleted by hand on the participant's request (`npm run db:delete-participant`, `apps/api/src/delete-participant.ts`): qando keeps no participant's email, so the request names the vote by the edit link or by the event's link and the name.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                                                                            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deleteExpired(db, now)`, `DeletedCounts` (`delete-expired.ts`)                                                                   | Deletes in one transaction, by the clock given: the events whose date passed 6 months ago (the last day of the confirmed option, or the deadline when none was confirmed, counted in the event's time zone: confirmed for 18 July 2026, deleted on 19 January 2027) with everything under them; what is left of the events cancelled 6 months ago; then, through `deleteNoLongerKept` of `apps/api/src/modules/auth`, the unused accounts left with no event (so an account goes in the same run as its last event), the expired codes and sessions, and what applications were given that can no longer be used. An event being changed while it runs (a confirmation, a new deadline) is skipped and left for the next run, and the events it holds are checked again before they are deleted, so a confirmation made meanwhile keeps its event by its confirmed date. Answers how many events, cancelled events and accounts it deleted. Deleting again deletes nothing more, so two runs at once or a run cut off are harmless. |
| `deleteParticipant(db, request, confirmed)`, `VoterRequest`, `IdentifiedVote`, `ParticipantDeletion` (`participant-deletion.ts`)  | Finds the one vote a `VoterRequest` identifies (the event's ID and an edit link's token, or the event's ID and a name) and, when `confirmed`, deletes it with its answers, leaving the event and its other votes as they are. One transaction holds the event's row `FOR UPDATE`, so a vote being cast or changed (which holds it `FOR SHARE`) is stored before the votes are read, and none is cast or renamed until the deletion ends. An edit link identifies its own vote only; a name the event's one vote with that name (`sameVoterName` of `packages/domain`), and none on an anonymous event. Answers the vote (`found` or `deleted`, its name, `null` on an anonymous event, and when it was cast) or why none: `no event` (no event has the link), `cancelled`, `anonymous` (a name for an anonymous event), `no vote`, `several` (with how many have the name). Deleting again finds no vote.                                                                   |
| `readScriptArguments(args)`, `ScriptArguments`, `usage`, `describeDeletion(request, deletion)` (`participant-deletion-script.ts`) | What `npm run db:delete-participant` reads and says: the request from a link (an edit link, or an event's link to vote followed by the voter's name, its words in any number of arguments; on any host, with or without its scheme) and `--yes` anywhere, or the problem with them, shown above `usage`; and the sentence that says each outcome.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

**Depends on:** `apps/api/src`, `apps/api/src/db`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`, `packages/domain`.

**Used by:** `apps/api/src`.

### `apps/web`

**Summary:** Web app (Angular 22).

**Purpose:** The pages people use. Calls the API under `/api` (proxied to `localhost:3000` locally) with the types of the contract.

**Contents:** `src/`, `public/`; `angular.json`, `proxy.conf.json` (sends `/api`, `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, each with or without a path after it, to the local API, as `render.yaml` does on Render), the Vitest and Stryker settings, and the mutation testing's test runner (`stryker-spec-files.mjs`: StrykerJS's Vitest runner reporting each test in the spec file it is written in, so an incremental run reuses the results of the tests whose spec did not change).

**Depends on:** `packages/contracts`, `packages/domain`.

**Used by:** `e2e`.

### `apps/web/public`

**Summary:** Static files served as they are.

**Purpose:** Files copied unchanged into the build.

**Contents:** `email/`; `icon.png`, `favicon.ico`, `logo.svg`. `icon.png` (qando's symbol, 192 px) is the icon `src/index.html` names, for browsers and search engines alike: search engines kept the framework's old picture under `favicon.ico`, the address it had before, so the icon has an address of its own, to keep from now on. `favicon.ico` (the same symbol, 16 to 256 px) stays for whoever asks for it by its usual address.

**Depends on:** —

**Used by:** `apps/web/src`.

### `apps/web/public/email`

**Summary:** Images the emails show.

**Purpose:** An email links its images by their full address, so the site serves them at `/email/…`, as PNG (many email clients do not show SVG). Mail clients keep a copy of each image by its address (Gmail's and Apple Mail's proxies), so each file carries in its name the first 8 hex characters of its content's SHA-256: a new image is a new file, and the email that links it changes its address. The API and the site deploy separately, so a new file reaches the site in a pull request of its own before an email links it; otherwise an email sent between the two deploys links a file the site does not have yet.

**Contents:** `logo-c75530c8.png` (qando's symbol, the two shapes without the word; twice the size the emails show it, for sharp screens).

**Depends on:** —

**Used by:** `apps/api/src/email` (the emails' shared frame links it).

### `apps/web/src/app/core`

**Summary:** App-wide services.

**Purpose:** What every page relies on and exists once in the app: access to the API, the session and what goes with it (the private pages' guard and their way to the sign-in page once the session ends, the management tokens kept, where signing in comes back to), translations, the header.
