### `apps/web/src/app/core/api`

**Summary:** Typed access to the API contract.

**Purpose:** Pages name an endpoint of the contract and get its typed, schema-checked answer; a contract change breaks the build of every page that uses it.

**Exports:**

| Export                                              | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apiResource(endpoint, params)` (`api-resource.ts`) | Reads a GET endpoint as a resource that follows the page: read again when its parameters change; its value is the checked success body.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `apiError(endpoint, error)` (`api-resource.ts`)     | The documented error answer behind a failed request, typed by its status; undefined when the API was not reached or the answer is not in the contract.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ApiClient` (`api-client.ts`)                       | `send(endpoint, request)` for the actions a page takes (send a vote): resolves with the checked success body, rejects with the HTTP error, or with a timeout once the time the request was given (`within`) has passed, the request given up.                                                                                                                             |
| `newCapabilityToken()` (`capability-token.ts`)      | A new capability token made by the page before its first send (a vote's, an event's): 128 random bits from the browser in base64url, so a repeated send carries the same token and stores nothing twice.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ApiRequest` (`api-client.ts`)                      | What a request carries: path parameters, headers and body, typed by the endpoint; and, optionally, `within`, the milliseconds the answer is waited for before the request is given up (no limit when absent).                                                                                                                                                             |
| `requestFailure(error)` (`request-failure.ts`)      | Follows the error a request or a resource failed with as a `RequestFailure` (null without one): a `429 RATE_LIMITED` counts its `Retry-After` seconds down each second, from the clock, and stays at 0; any other error, or a `429` that breaks the contract, is a plain failure. Runs in an injection context.                                                           |
| `RequestFailure` (`request-failure.ts`)             | How a request failed, as a page tells it: `failed` (trying again may work now) or `limited` with the `seconds` still to wait.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `waiting(failure)` (`request-failure.ts`)           | A rate limit with seconds left: sending again now would be refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `secondsUntil(until)` (`wait.ts`)                   | The whole seconds left until a clock time in milliseconds (null: nothing to wait for), as a signal counted down each second from the clock, so a tab whose timers were held back still shows the time left; 0 once the time has come, and without one; a new time starts again. `requestFailure` counts with it. Runs in an injection context, whose end stops the count. |

**Depends on:** `packages/contracts`.

**Used by:** `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`, `apps/web/src/app/features/connect`, `apps/web/src/app/features/create`, `apps/web/src/app/features/manage`, `apps/web/src/app/features/my-events`, `apps/web/src/app/features/results`, `apps/web/src/app/features/sign-in`, `apps/web/src/app/features/vote`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`.

### `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`

**Summary:** The session, the private pages' guard and their way to the sign-in page once the session ends, the management tokens kept, where signing in comes back to, an application's request to connect in a page's address and the browser's own navigation.

**Purpose:** What the browser knows of its organizer: which account is signed in (asked to the API, as the page cannot read the session cookie), signing out, the guard that keeps the private pages for an account signed in, and the management tokens the browser keeps until it signs out. Also the one place that knows how a page asks the sign-in page to come back to it (the `returnTo` query of `/sign-in`) and which page signing in opens, so the link that asks and the page that answers cannot disagree. Of a `returnTo`, only a path of qando is ever followed. Also how a page reads from its own address the request to connect an application that it was opened with (`connectionRequestOf`): the sign-in page and the consent page are both opened with one, and each sends it on as the same text. And the browser's own navigation (`WholeNavigation`), through which a page leaves the app for an address its router does not serve: a service, so that tests replace it with a recorder and stay on their page. Also what a private page does when its session ends while it is open (`signInAgainOnceEnded`): it goes to the sign-in page, which comes back to it.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                     | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signInFrom(url)` (`sign-in-return.ts`)                                    | The query of a link to the sign-in page from the page at `url` (path and query), so that signing in comes back to it: `{ returnTo }`, nothing from the home page, and from the sign-in page its own query, whole: what it was already asked, a page to come back to or an application's request to connect with every parameter, so a link to the sign-in page pressed on that page leaves it as it is and drops no request. The answer is the router's `Params`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `returnTarget(returnTo)` (`sign-in-return.ts`)                             | The page to open after signing in, from the sign-in page's `returnTo`: that page when it is one of qando's other than the home and the sign-in pages, "Mis eventos" (`/my-events`) otherwise; an address of another site is never followed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Session` (`session.ts`)                                                   | The organizer's session on this browser. `account`: a signal of the account signed in (`SignedInAccount`, `packages/contracts/src/auth`), `undefined` until the API first answers (`GET /api/auth/session`, asked when the app starts), `null` without a session. `answered`: a signal of whether `account` is the API's answer, false until it first answers and while the last question got no answer (`account` is then `null` all the same). `signedIn()`: whether an account is signed in, once the API has answered; a question the API could not answer counts as no session and is asked again here. `refresh()`: asks the API again, as after signing in. `signOut()`: the server ends the session (`POST /api/auth/sign-out`), then the browser forgets the account and every management token it keeps (`ManagementTokens.forgetAll`; the voters' tokens stay); rejects, with nothing forgotten, when the server could not end it. `sendDeletionCode()`: emails the account the code that deletes it (`POST /api/me/deletion-code`); answers the seconds until another may be asked, and rejects, with nothing forgotten, when it was not sent. `deleteAccount(code)`: the server deletes the account with all its events and ends its sessions (`POST /api/me/deletion`), then the browser forgets it as when signing out; answers how many events went with it, and rejects, with nothing forgotten, when it was not deleted (a refused code among the reasons) or its answer was lost or took over 20 seconds. Both answer `null` when the server knew no session any more (`401`), which the browser then forgets as when signing out; a `401` that arrives once the session was asked again or forgotten meanwhile (another tab signed in) rejects instead, forgetting nothing. Only the answer to the last question or sign-out is kept. The browser's tabs share the session: a tab that signs in (`refresh()`) or out (also by deleting its account) tells the others (`BroadcastChannel`), which ask again or forget as if it had happened in them. |
| `signedInOnly` (`signed-in-only.ts`), guard of `/my-events`, `/connected-apps` and `/profile` | Opens the private pages for an account signed in (`Session.signedIn`); sends anyone else to `/sign-in?returnTo=<the page asked for>` (`signInFrom`), so signing in comes back to it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `signInAgainOnceEnded(ended, from)` (`session-ended.ts`) | Called in a private page's constructor: once `ended()` is true (the API answered the page `401`: the session ended since the page opened), it has `Session` ask the API again (`refresh`), so the header shows "Entrar", and then opens the sign-in page with `returnTo` set to `from` (`signInFrom`), so that signing in comes back to the page; unless the page was left meanwhile (the logo, "Cerrar sesión"): the user's choice stands. "Mis eventos" (`apps/web/src/app/features/my-events`) and "Apps conectadas" (`apps/web/src/app/features/connected-apps`) call it. |
| `ManagementTokens` (`management-tokens.ts`)                                | The management tokens this browser keeps, one per event whose management link it opened: in its storage (shared by its tabs, kept after a reload), or for the page alone when the browser refuses its storage (private windows, blocked site data). `keep(eventId, token)` keeps the event's token in the place of the one kept before; `of(eventId)` answers it, `null` when none is kept; `forgetAll()` forgets every one, in every tab, as signing out does, so a shared computer keeps no way into anyone's events (the links stay in their emails).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `connectionRequestOf(query)` (`connection-request.ts`) | The request to connect an application that a page was opened with, from the query of the page's address (the router's `ParamMap`): the whole query, every value of each name, as the API takes it, when it carries what a request always does (`response_type`, `client_id`) or the authorization server's signature (`sig`); none otherwise. Any one of them is enough: what is left of a request whose address was cut short is still sent, and the API says what it is worth, so the person is told to start again instead of nothing. Both pages the authorization server opens with a request read it here: the sign-in page (`apps/web/src/app/features/sign-in`), which sends it with the sign-in, and the consent page (`apps/web/src/app/features/connect`), which asks which application it names and sends it with the account's answer. |
| `WholeNavigation` (`whole-navigation.ts`)                                   | The browser's own navigation, for an address the app's router does not serve: one of the API's, which answers by sending the browser on, or another site's. `replaceWith(address)` loads `address` in place of the current page, so going back does not return to it. Tests replace it with a recorder.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

**Depends on:** `apps/web/src/app/core/api`, `packages/contracts`.

**Used by:** `apps/web/src/app` (routes), `apps/web/src/app/core/layout`, `apps/web/src/app/features/connect`, `apps/web/src/app/features/connected-apps`, `apps/web/src/app/features/create`, `apps/web/src/app/features/manage`, `apps/web/src/app/features/my-events`, `apps/web/src/app/features/sign-in`.

### `apps/web/src/app/core/layout`

**Summary:** The header of every page, with the account's menu, and the keyboard-only focus ring of text fields; the waves behind every page in `waves-background/`.

**Purpose:** The page frame that is not a page, and what every page's text fields share about focus.

**Components:**

| Component                                                            | Inputs → outputs                            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **`AppHeader`** (`app-header.*`)                                     | —                                           | The logo back to the home page and, at the other end, what `Session.account` (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) says: `AccountMenu` for an account signed in; without a session the "Entrar" icon, which links to `/sign-in` with `returnTo` set to the page it is pressed on, so that signing in comes back to it (nothing from the home page, and on the sign-in page that page's own query, so the link leaves it as it is and an application's request to connect is not dropped; `signInFrom`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`); neither until the session is known, so "Entrar" never shows for a moment to someone signed in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **`AccountMenu`** (`account-menu.*`), `app-account-menu`             | `account` (the `SignedInAccount`, required) | The account signed in: a round button with its initial (the first character, in capitals, of its name, or of its email while it has no name), named "Cuenta de <name or email>", that opens a small menu under it (220 px wide, up to 310 px; a longer email is cut with "…") with the account's email, "Mis eventos" (`/my-events`), "Apps conectadas" (`/connected-apps`), "Privacidad y condiciones" (`/privacy`, in the same tab) and "Cerrar sesión". A red trash at the end of the email's row, named "Eliminar mi cuenta" (said under it, in red, by a `Tooltip` while the mouse is over it; with a mouse shown only while it is over the row or the trash has the focus, always on a phone), closes the menu and opens `AccountDeletion` (its code loaded apart from the app's first, `@defer`, fetched once the page is idle). The menu closes with Escape (the focus back on the button), with a press or the focus anywhere else, and once something is chosen. "Cerrar sesión" calls `Session.signOut` (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`), then opens the home page with the toast "Has cerrado sesión." (`Toaster`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`); when the server could not end the session the page stays as it is and the toast says "No se ha podido cerrar sesión. Inténtalo de nuevo." |
| **`AccountDeletion`** (`account-deletion.*`), `app-account-deletion` | `email` (required) → `closed`               | Deleting the signed-in account, in a `Dialog` with its own answers, in two steps. The question "¿Eliminar tu cuenta?" says what goes with it (all its events; their links will say the page does not exist) and that a code goes to `email`; "Enviar código" (red; "Enviando…" while on its way) sends the code (`Session.sendDeletionCode`) and, when it could not, says "No se ha podido enviar el código. Inténtalo de nuevo." under it. Then a `CodeStep` (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) in the dialog's look, with "Tu cuenta se eliminará al escribir la última cifra." and "Eliminando…": the last digit calls `Session.deleteAccount`, then the home page opens with the toast "Se han eliminado tu cuenta y tus eventos." ("Se ha eliminado tu cuenta." with none); a new code is sent the same way. "Volver" closes it from either step; while the code is checked nothing closes it (the `Dialog` `held`, "Volver" off). When the server knew no session any more (either request answered `null`), the home page opens with the toast "Se ha cerrado tu sesión. Si al volver a entrar no ves tus eventos, tu cuenta ya se eliminó.".                                                                                                               |

**Exports:**

| Export                                             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provideKeyboardFocusRing()` (`keyboard-focus.ts`) | Text fields show the focus ring only when a key brought the focus to them, never on load, by a click or by a tap. It remembers whether the last interaction was a key or a pointer and, each time the focus moves, marks `<html>` with `data-keyboard-focus` when a key brought it; `apps/web/src/styles` (`_base.scss`) draws the text-field ring only under that mark. Typing never changes the mark. Other controls keep the browser's own `:focus-visible`. |

**Depends on:** `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`, `packages/contracts`.

**Used by:** `apps/web/src/app`.

### `apps/web/src/app/core/layout/waves-background`

**Summary:** The animated waves behind every page.

**Purpose:** Cream and green ribbons with contour lines on a paper grain, drawn as SVG behind every page: still until the mouse or a finger moves over the bare page, then rippling around the pointer and settling about 1.5 s after it stops. Nothing that paints its own background (cards, dialogs) makes them move; with a finger, what counts is what is under it now (`document.elementFromPoint`), not where the touch began. Frames run only while something moves, only the ribbons that changed are redrawn, and no change detection runs per frame.

**Components:**

| Component                                                            | Inputs → outputs | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **`WavesBackground`** (`waves-background.*`), `app-waves-background` | —                | Placed last in the `App` shell (`apps/web/src/app`), after the toast, so its button comes last in the reading order. A fixed layer `100lvh` tall, `--q-page-bg` until drawn, with `wideWaves` on every screen, cropped to cover (`xMidYMid slice`), so a resized or turned screen only scales and crops it (an upright phone shows its central strip). With a mouse the waves start paused: a line icon in the lower left corner (play or pause in a circle, as the header's sign-in icon) starts them, rippling the waves around it at once, and pauses them ("Animar el fondo" / "Pausar la animación del fondo"); starting them is remembered on the device (`localStorage`, `qando.backgroundPlaying`). A touch screen has no button and its waves follow the finger; `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` keeps them still and hides the button, also when it changes while the page is open. |

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                        | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WaveField`, `LayerShape` (`wave-field.ts`)                                   | The motion as pure state: `pointerAt(point)`, `pointerGone()`, `ripple(point)` (the waves around a point stirred at once, as a quick pass of the pointer), `advance(ms)` returns the changed `LayerShape`s (`{ layer, ribbon, lines }`), `shapes()` all of them, `still` whether nothing moves. Fixed 60 Hz steps, so a 120 Hz screen moves the same; a late frame advances at most 100 ms. |
| `ribbonPath`, `contourPath`, `toScene` (`wave-geometry.ts`)                   | Pure geometry: a ribbon's SVG path between two edges, a contour line through its points (Catmull-Rom as cubic Béziers), and a screen point turned into a drawing point under `slice`.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Point`, `WaveLayer`, `WaveComposition`, `wideWaves` (`wave-compositions.ts`) | The drawing as data: one wide composition (1600×900) for every screen, layer by layer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

**Depends on:** `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui` (`TOUCH_QUERY`), `apps/web/src/i18n`, `apps/web/src/styles`.

**Used by:** `apps/web/src/app`.

### `apps/web/src/app/features/connect`

**Summary:** The consent page, where an account allows an application to act for it.

**Purpose:** The page the authorization server (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`) sends a signed-in browser to when an application, an AI assistant, asks to act for its account: it names the application by what it says of itself (its name and the host it is published at, never a logo), says for which account it asks and what it will be able to do, and takes one answer, "Permitir" or "Cancelar", after which the browser goes back to the application. The application's request, signed by the authorization server and valid 10 minutes, is the query of the page's address: the page sends it on whole, and the API says what it is worth. The card is the sign-in page's, as the consent is asked where signing in was: its texts are the stylesheet partial `_sign-in-texts.scss` and its two buttons a dialog's answers, `_answers.scss` (`apps/web/src/styles`). Its copy is `connect` in the catalogue (`apps/web/src/i18n/es.json`).

**Components:**

| Component | Inputs → outputs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`ConnectPage`** (`connect-page.*`), route `/connect` | — | Reads the request to connect from its address when it is created (`connectionRequestOf`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) and asks `ConnectionConsent.application` which application it names; meanwhile `LoadingState` (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) stands where the card will, in its own card. Then the card, for an application that calls itself Claude: the heading "Conectar Claude con qando" (the page's `h1`, which takes the focus so that it is read), "Claude (claude.ai) quiere usar tu cuenta ana@example.com.", with the host it is published at and the email of the account the session holds (`Session.account`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`), "Podrá:" and what the application will be able to do (see the account's events and their results; create events and manage them), a hint to allow it only when qando has just been added in that application, the two answers side by side, "Cancelar" and "Permitir", and `PrivacyLink`. The application's name and host are its own text, of any length: always shown as text, and broken wherever they must. The account named is the one the session holds at each moment, not the one it held when the page loaded, as the answer is taken for that account, whichever tab signed it in: another account signed in from another tab changes the card. Either button sends the answer once through `ConnectionConsent.answer`, both off meanwhile, and the page then gives the address answered, the application's, to the browser through `WholeNavigation.replaceWith` (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`). For a page's address the buttons stay off until the browser has left; for an address the browser does not leave for (`stays`: an application installed on the computer, which the browser hands the address to), a card takes the consent's place, "Vuelve a Claude", "Hemos enviado tu respuesta a Claude. Si no se ha abierto, prueba de nuevo." and "Abrir Claude", which hands the same address to the browser again: the answer is given once, since a "Cancelar" after a "Permitir" would tell the application it was refused while the allowance the authorization server stored stays. An answer that could not be sent is told under the buttons (`FailureNotice`: "No se ha podido enviar tu respuesta. Inténtalo de nuevo.", or the time to wait of a rate limit, the buttons off until it has passed). A page opened without a request, or whose request has expired when it is asked about or answered, shows "Esta solicitud ha caducado", "Vuelve a tu asistente y empieza la conexión otra vez." and a link to "Mis eventos". When the account is gone while the card shows (signed out from another tab, or a question about the session that failed: the card gives way to `LoadingState`), the page asks the API again what to show, as when it opened; an answer given meanwhile stands, and what was learned is dropped. When the session has ended (found when asking or when answering), it has `Session` ask the API again (`refresh`), so the header shows "Entrar", and gives its place in the browser's history to the sign-in page with its whole query, which comes back with the request, unless the person has left the page meanwhile. When the page could not load (a question that failed, or an account the app's session does not know), `ErrorState` stands where the card will, in its own card, the one `LoadingState` draws, with "Reintentar" (a rate limit counted down). |

**Exports:**

| Export | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `ConnectionConsent` (`connection-consent.ts`) | A request to connect an application, as the consent page deals with it; both methods take the request whole, as the page's address carries it. `application(connectionRequest)` answers the application the request names, what it says of itself to show the account (`ConnectingApplication`, `packages/contracts/src/auth`), asked of `POST /api/auth/connecting-application` through `ApiClient` (`apps/web/src/app/core/api`). `answer(connectionRequest, allow)` sends the account's answer, to allow the application or not, to the authorization server's own route (`POST /api/auth/oauth2/consent`, which is not in the API's contract) and answers `{ returnTo, stays }`: `returnTo`, where the browser goes on either way, back to the application with the access or the refusal; and `stays`, whether the browser stays on the consent page once it is given that address: false for a page's address (`http:`, `https:`), which the browser opens in place of the page it shows, and true for any other address the browser takes, an application installed on the computer, which the browser hands the address to while it stays on the consent page. Either method answers a `NothingToAllow` instead when the request has nothing to allow any more; any other failure rejects with the error itself (an HTTP error, whose rate limit the page can then count down). An address the browser would run or draw by itself instead of opening it (`javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `blob:`) is never answered, nor is an answer without an address: `answer` rejects. |
| `NothingToAllow` (`connection-consent.ts`) | Why a request to connect has nothing to allow any more: `'expired'` (the authorization server did not sign it, or signed it more than 10 minutes ago: the API's `410`, the consent route's `400` with `invalid_signature`) or `'signed-out'` (the session that was to answer it has ended: `401` from either). |

**Depends on:** `apps/web/src/styles`, `apps/web/src/app/core/api`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`, `packages/contracts/src/auth`.

**Used by:** `apps/web/src/app` (routes).

### `apps/web/src/app/features/connected-apps`

**Summary:** "Apps conectadas", the applications the signed-in account allowed, and disconnecting them.

**Purpose:** The private page where an account sees the applications (AI assistants) it allowed to act for it, named as the consent page (`apps/web/src/app/features/connect`) named them, and disconnects any of them, which ends that application's access at once; the account menu (`AccountMenu`, `apps/web/src/app/core/layout`) links to it. Its card is the one of "Mis eventos" (`apps/web/src/app/features/my-events`), the stylesheet partial `_list-card.scss` (`apps/web/src/styles`): the heading, then a row per application between thin lines, its name over its state line, with "Desconectar" at its end, beside its texts while they keep their least room (`--q-row-text-min`) and under them where they would not. With no application, the page says how to connect one and gives the connector's address in a white well, as the management page's links (`_wells.scss`, `apps/web/src/styles`). Its copy is `connectedApps` in the catalogue (`apps/web/src/i18n/es.json`).

**Components:**

| Component | Inputs → outputs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`ConnectedAppsPage`** (`connected-apps-page.*`), route `/connected-apps` (private: `signedInOnly`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`; tab title "Apps conectadas") | — | Reads `GET /api/me/connected-apps` (`apiResource(connectedApplicationsEndpoint)`, `apps/web/src/app/core/api`) and shows loading (`LoadingState`), the error with "Reintentar" (`ErrorState`, both `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) or the card under the heading "Apps conectadas". With applications, the line "Asistentes de IA que pueden ver y gestionar tus eventos por ti." and a row per application, the newest connection first: its name over "claude.ai · Conectada el 24 de noviembre de 2026" (its host, and the day by `longDate`, `apps/web/src/app/features/vote`, in the browser's time zone), and "Desconectar", an `AskFirstButton` (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) named "Desconectar <name>" that asks "¿Desconectar?" in its place. Its "Sí" sends `DELETE /api/me/connected-apps/{id}` (`disconnectApplicationEndpoint`, through `ApiClient`, `apps/web/src/app/core/api`), one request per connection at a time: on `200`, or `404` (a connection the account no longer has: disconnected or connected again from another tab, or another account signed in there), the row leaves, and the focus goes to the heading, the place where the list starts again, unless the user moved it elsewhere meanwhile; on `404` the list is also read again; any failure other than `401` keeps the row, and the toast says "No se ha podido desconectar. Inténtalo de nuevo." (`Toaster`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`). With none, "No tienes ninguna aplicación conectada." and `ConnectorAddress`. When either request is answered `401` (the session ended since the page opened) it shows loading, not the error, and `signInAgainOnceEnded` (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) opens the sign-in page, which comes back here, unless the user has left the page meanwhile. An answer that comes once the page is left changes nothing. |
| **`ConnectorAddress`** (`connector-address.*`), `app-connector-address` | — | How to connect an assistant: "Para conectar un asistente, añade qando en sus ajustes de conectores con esta dirección:", then the connector's address in full (the page's origin and `connectorPath`, `packages/contracts/src/auth`, as `https://qando.app/api/mcp`) in a white well, as the management page's links, with "Copiar", which copies it with `LinkCopier` (`apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`): the toast "Enlace copiado"; refused by the browser, nothing, the address staying on screen. |

**Depends on:** `apps/web/src/styles`, `apps/web/src/app/core/api`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`, `apps/web/src/app/features/vote`, `packages/contracts/src/auth`.

**Used by:** `apps/web/src/app` (routes).

### `apps/web/src/app/features/create`

**Summary:** The event creation wizard.

**Purpose:** The home page, where an organizer creates an event: the steps as a stack of cards (`StepStack`), the page holding what each step asks so a step that folds into its tab and comes back loses nothing. Step 1 (the event's title) and step 2 (the dates, marked on a month calendar that goes from today to twelve months ahead: days one by one, and ranges, days in a row proposed as one option, which can be saved to mark their days again; 60 options at most, and a trash that clears them all) are built, and so are the times of the dates, a step of its own only while times are asked for and a date of its own can have them (a column of hours a day, where each time marked is one more option), and then, in their place in the same card, their summary, every option as it will be voted, on the same columns; and the last step, named "último paso", the deadline in three selects, day, month and year (`DeadlineField`), a note, anonymous voting, the organizer's name (`OrganizerNameField`), the email and "Crear", which creates the event for the organizer signed in (`WizardFinish`) and leaves "¡Hecho!" in the wizard's place (`CreateDone`). The times step and the summary share their window on a row of columns (`ColumnStrip`, `columnsOnScreen`) and the Sass partial of a step of columns (`_column-step.scss`: the label, the window between the years of its days, the row and a column, and the options counter over the arrows); the summary draws its boxes of times with the voting page's (`_time-blocks.scss`, `apps/web/src/app/features/vote`); the last step and its name field share the look of the step's labels (`_last-step.scss`). The smart calendar of the dates step is built: a switch opens a box over the calendar (`PhraseBox`) where the dates are asked for in plain words; the API reads the phrase (`PhraseReader`), what it gives takes the place of the dates chosen (`markingOf`), and the lines that tell what could not be marked as it was said (`noticeLines`) show in an amber box (`NoticeBox`). Where the browser can take dictation, the phrase can also be said to the box's microphone (`Dictation`).

A press on a free day marks it as a date of its own (`pressDay`), also next to a marked one; a press on a marked day removes it, and on any day of a range, the whole range. Either way stops at the day next to another range, takes in the dates of their own on the way and, begun on the first or the last day of a range, moves that end; begun on a day between them it does nothing. The day held, pressed again or left held when going on with "Siguiente", stays as a date of its own. A double-click is two presses. While a drag goes on, nothing else marks or holds a day, nor does "Siguiente" go on (a key, another finger); the month can still change. A range is drawn as one band (its ends as dates, the days between fainter, cut with white dashes where it goes on in another week; two ranges that touch are seen as two) and the mouse over any of its days darkens it whole; while a range is being made, its first day is dark, the days on the way carry a thin ring and the day reached a thick one, with a small arrow at the side of its row the range goes towards. A range is saved with its "+" (`saveRange`), a small round button on the corner of its last day on screen (its last day, or the month's when the range goes on into the next month; it saves the whole range) named with its range for screen readers ("Guardar el rango del 17 de junio al 19 de junio"): the range leaves the calendar, its days free again under a pale band (`GridDay.saved`), and waits under the calendar as a pill ("Mié 17 ➔ Vie 19"; the pills are `SavedPills`, which draws in each what the step's template says and takes from the step the tip and the name of its "−"), the focus going to the day the "+" was on; a range made again over the days of a saved one, from its first to its last (`Drag.alreadySaved`), changes nothing, whatever is marked on those days, and pins the pill of that saved range, which shows it is there already; the click of that same press does not let the pill go. A mouse finds the "+" over any day of its range, though not while it rests on the day the drag that made the range was released on (released off the days, `DayDrop.onDay`, the "+" shows as soon as the mouse comes back); the keyboard, with Tab from a day of the range; without a mouse (`(hover: none), (pointer: coarse)`) a button on the right under the calendar ("Guardar un rango", there while a range has a day on screen) gives way to the "+" of every range, red (`--q-engaged`) and the first with the focus, its row keeping its height: they hide, and the button is back, when the ranges change, as when one is saved, on a press anywhere but on one of them (whatever is pressed does what it does), when a drag begins or a day is held, and on Escape, the button taking the focus; the button is red while it is pressed; no "+" is there while a range is being made. The pills are the saved ranges with a day in the month on screen, under a title that says how to see them ("Pasa el ratón para visualizar estas fechas.", or "Toca un rango para verlo en el calendario." without a mouse). The mouse over a pill outlines its range on the calendar; a press on the pill pins it (`GridDay.viewed`: a filled band over whatever its days have, its two ends bold and the days between faint), until Escape, the pill again, another pill (which is pinned instead) or a press anywhere else on the page, which on a day of the view does nothing more and on another day acts as usual; the month arrows keep the view while its range has days in the month, a day held with Shift+Enter or a drag lets it go, and it is let go by itself once its range is no longer saved; pinned days do not answer the mouse. A pill's "−" deletes its range at once (`removeSaved`), the focus going to the pill that takes its place, the last one, or the calendar: a mouse and the keyboard find it on the pill while none is pinned; without a mouse it is there only on the pinned pill; nothing is deleted while a drag goes on. Each date of its own, each range and each saved range is one option of the event, which takes `MAX_OPTIONS` (60, `packages/domain/src`): from 50 on, a counter in the middle of the row under the calendar says how many are taken (`OptionCounter`), red and bold at 60, when a press on a free day leaves it free and a drag that would leave one option more leaves nothing (`pressDay`, `dragDays`); Shift+Enter still holds a free day (`holdDay`), for a range that takes dates of their own in, and pressed again or followed by a range that would be one option more it stays free. That row is always there, so nothing under it moves when what it holds comes and goes: on its left the trash (`AskFirstButton`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`), there while a date is marked or a range saved, which, once its question is answered "Sí", clears every date, range and saved range and lets go of a day held, the month staying and the focus going to the calendar (nothing is cleared while a drag goes on); on its right, without a mouse, the "Guardar un rango" button. The month arrows repeat while held down (`HoldRepeat`) and grow and darken under the mouse, as the other small arrows of the wizard. A finger that slides sideways over the days before it has rested on one (`SideSlide`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) moves them with it, the months beside drawn next to them for the eye only (spans, no buttons), never farther than a month nor past the first or the last month; when it lifts the calendar goes to the month it brought more than a quarter of its width into sight, or to the one it was flung towards, and back otherwise, the days gliding there from where the finger left them (a CSS animation from `--glide-from`; at once with reduced motion); a slide begun while they still glide takes them from where they are drawn. The month arrows, the keyboard and a drag's rest at a side change the month at once, as before. The days before today and after the last day an event can propose (`latestOptionDate`, `packages/domain/src`) are grey and cannot be pressed; the month arrows stop, dimmed but still focusable, at the current month and at the month of that last day. Today is read from the clock again when the step is entered and on every use (a press, a month arrow, a key, a day held, a drag's release, "Siguiente"): after midnight the dates marked before the new today leave `selection` (`withoutDatesBefore`: a range that began before it, marked or saved, leaves whole), a day held before it, or on a range that began before it, is let go, a drag with a day before it (also the first day of a range dragged by its end) leaves nothing, and `month` is never left before today's month. With the keyboard, Tab reaches one day (the one used last, or the first that can be pressed), the arrow keys move by day and by week, into the next or the previous month too, PageUp and PageDown change the month keeping the day, and Enter or Space press the day; each day is named in full for screen readers ("sábado, 20 de junio"), a day of a range with its range ("sábado, 20 de junio, rango del 18 de junio al 20 de junio"). Until a date is marked or a range saved, "Siguiente" does nothing, though it stays in the Tab order, and tells screen readers why ("Selecciona al menos una fecha."). Below 650 px the calendar reaches the card's sides and each day is as tall as it is wide. The "Horario" switch reads the selection's `timed` and writes it with `withTimesAsked`, so turning it off forgets the times marked; the counter and the stop at 60 count the times of the dates (`optionCount`), and the trash keeps the switch as it was (`withoutDates`). The step asks "¿Cuándo?" (the `step-question` mixin, `apps/web/src/styles`, as the times step's "¿A qué hora?"), and beside it the sparkles are the button of the smart calendar, named "Generar fechas con IA" (`aria-pressed`, not pressed whenever the step is entered), red and a little larger under the mouse, as the trash, and while the box is open, when a press closes it; under the mouse they say their name over them (`Tooltip`), until pressed. Pressed, `PhraseBox` covers the calendar, which stays in the page under it, unseen and `inert`, both in one grid cell, so the box is as large as the calendar (larger only when its text and notices need more) and nothing under them moves; a day held is let go. The open box's "X", "Cerrar el calendario inteligente", in its top right corner, closes it and gives the focus to the sparkles. What is under the calendar stays: the pills, the row and the two round arrows, though without a mouse the "Guardar un rango" button is not shown meanwhile, and the arrow that goes on is "Generar fechas" (a calendar with a plus), which has the box's phrase read (`PhraseBox.generate`) and says it is disabled, still in the Tab order, while there is nothing to send or an answer is waited for (`PhraseBox.ready`). A phrase that gives dates (`marked`) closes the box: they take the place of every date, range and saved range chosen before, `month` goes to the month of the first day marked (`firstMarked`), the focus goes to the calendar, and what the reading tells shows above the calendar (`NoticeBox`, in a `status` region that is always in the page) until its cross, the trash or the next phrase that gives dates; it is not shown while the box is open. With the box open the trash is also there for a text alone and empties the box with the dates (`PhraseBox.clear`: its text and what it tells go, an answer waited for is dropped and marks nothing when it comes, and the focus is on the text box); with the box closed a text alone has no trash, and the trash of the dates clears a text kept too. When a phrase's dates take the place of others, a message at the bottom of the screen (`Toaster.offer`) says how many, each date, range and saved range as one ("Hemos sustituido las 3 fechas que tenías marcadas.", or "la fecha" for one), with "Deshacer": it puts back the dates, their times and the month as they were before the phrase, takes away what the phrase told, lets go a day held and brings the calendar back with the focus, the box closed. The offer goes once the dates change in any way (a press, the "Horario" switch, the trash, midnight) and when the step folds away; after two phrases it undoes the second. |
| **`PhraseBox`** (`phrase-box.*`), with `PhraseMarked`                                                                                                                          | `text` (model, required: the phrase as written), `timed` (required: times were asked for before the phrase, and stay asked for whatever it says), `timeZone` (optional: the zone the phrase is read in; the browser's without one) → `marked` (`PhraseMarked`: the `selection` the phrase leaves, in place of the one before, and the `lines` that tell about it, none for a plain reading)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The box of the smart calendar: a text box that grows with what is written (120 characters at most, counted under it, "0/120"), named for screen readers and with an example, which takes the focus when the box opens. Enter has the phrase read (`PhraseReader`); with Shift, or while a character is being composed, it writes. Whoever shows the box can have the phrase read with `generate()`, ask `ready` (a signal: there is a phrase that is not blank and no answer is waited for, so `generate()` would send it) and empty it with `clear()`: its text, its questions and what it tells go, the answer waited for is dropped, and the text box takes the focus. While the answer is waited for a spinner turns and screen readers hear "Generando fechas…"; nothing else is sent meanwhile. A phrase that gives dates is told through `marked` (`markingOf`, `noticeLines`) and leaves nothing in the box; when it says a time without its half of the day ("a las 8"), the box first asks which is meant, under the text (`TimeQuestions`), tells nothing until the last question is answered, and loses the questions to the next phrase sent or to `clear()`; one that gives none stays with why, in amber (`NoticeBox`, in a `status` region); one that could not be read, with a red line ("No se ha podido interpretar", or "Demasiadas peticiones, inténtalo en un momento", in an `alert` region). Both go with their cross or as soon as the next phrase is sent. An answer no longer waited for, because the box was emptied or is gone, is dropped when it comes. Where the browser can take dictation the text's well has a microphone at its end (`Dictation`), which writes what is heard into the text; it stops listening when the phrase is sent, when the box is emptied and when it closes, and a microphone the browser refuses is told with a red line ("Permiso de micrófono denegado. Actívalo en los ajustes del navegador."), which goes as the others. | **`DeadlineField`** (`deadline-field.*`)                                                                                                                                       | `value` (model, required: the deadline, `YYYY-MM-DD`), `labelledBy` (required: the ID of what names it), `timeZone`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | The deadline of an event, chosen with three selects in a row, its day, its month in words ("noviembre", `monthName` of `calendarWords`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) and its year, each a pill with a chevron, named together (a group) by the element of the page given (`labelledBy`: the wizard's question, the management page's help line) and each by its part ("Día", "Mes", "Año"). They offer only the dates from today to `latestOptionDate` (`packages/domain/src`): the days of the month shown, the months of the year shown and the years between. A part chosen that leaves the date out (31 January to February, December to a year that ends in November) moves it to the nearest date that can be chosen. Today is read from the clock when a select is reached and on every choice, in `timeZone` (the event's, on the management page) or else the person's own; a deadline that became yesterday at midnight is still shown until another is chosen. | `pressHour(day, hour, full)`, `dragHours(day, from, to, full)`, `shiftQuarter(day, hour, by, full)`, `saveTime(day, time)`, `removeSavedTime(day, time)`, `shiftEdited(day, edit, hour, by, full)`, `endEdit(day, edit, full)`, `withTimeRead(day, time)`, `savedLike(day, time)`, `timesOf(day)`, `optionsOf(day)`, `markAt(times, hour)`, `DayTimes`, `NO_TIMES`, `SavedEdit`, `DayTime`, `HourMark`, `HourDrag` (`day-times.ts`) | The times of one day, a `DayTimes`: the `marked` ones, in order and one an hour at most, and the `saved` ones, by when each starts and then by when it ends, no two alike, which can share hours with each other and with the marked ones (`NO_TIMES`: none). Each is a `DayTime` as an option carries its time: one time (`{ kind: 'single', at: 'HH:MM' }`) or a time range (`{ kind: 'range', start, end }`, two hours of the day at least, so it ends after it starts). Each different time is one option of the event, a marked time like a saved one the same option, and a day without times is one option: `timesOf` gives the different times in order and `optionsOf` how many options they are. When the event takes no more options (`full`), no rule leaves the day with one more: it answers the very same value, so a day without times still takes its first, and a time like a saved one is still marked. `pressHour`: an hour (0 to 23) with no time gains one on the hour, an hour with a time loses it, and any hour of a range removes the range. `dragHours`: a drag from an hour to another, up or down, makes one range of its hours, taking in the times of their own on the way and stopping at the hour next to another range; a drag of one hour is a time of its own; from a time the range keeps its minutes at that end; from an end of a range it moves that end, the other staying and each with its minutes, also when the range turns around; it answers a `HourDrag` (`drawn`, the time or range it draws, and `times`, the day's times with it among the marked), or `null` from an hour between the ends of a range and when it would add an option to a `full` event. `shiftQuarter`: the marked time of an hour, or the end of a range at that hour, moves a quarter later (`by` 1) or earlier (-1) and stops at :00 and :45 (the very same value there, on an hour with no time and between the ends of a range). `saveTime`: a marked time is no longer marked and is one of the saved, unless one like it is there already (the very same value for a time that is not marked). `removeSavedTime`: the times without a saved one. A saved time is edited through a `SavedEdit` (the time as it is `saved` and as it is `now`), which changes nothing of the day until it ends: `shiftEdited` moves it by quarters as `shiftQuarter` does a marked time (the very same edit at its stop and at any other hour), and `endEdit` saves it as it is now, in its place among the saved or gone into the one it has become like (the very same value when it ends as it was saved, and when a `full` event would get one option more from it: the edit is undone); an edit dropped is undone. `withTimeRead`: a time read from a phrase joins the times of the day, marked on its hours while they are free; when one of them has a time marked before, whichever of the two is a range is saved, so a time of its own takes the hour of the range marked there, and of two of a kind, the one read later; the very same value when one like it is there, marked or saved, and `null` for a range the hours of a day cannot hold (one within a single clock hour, `withinOneHour` of `packages/domain/src`, the rule every option follows). `savedLike`: the saved time like a time, itself when it is one of them or the one with its ends, or `null` when none is; after an edit has ended, what its saved time now is. `markAt`: what an hour is among a list of times, a `HourMark`: its `part` (`free`, `single`, `start`, `end` or `between`), its `time` and the `minutes` it shows (":15"). |

**Used by:** `apps/web/src/app`, `apps/web/src/app/features/manage`.

### `apps/web/src/app/features/manage`

**Summary:** The management page.

**Purpose:** The page the organizer opens with the management link: the event's title and state, the choice of its final date and its confirmation, the links to pass on, and the state of the emails it sends the organizer, with the retry of a failed one; each in a section that folds (`ManageSection`). The management token is taken from the link, kept per event in the browser (`ManagementTokens`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`) until it signs out, and sent in a header, never left in the address bar. Until a date is confirmed, its deadline: changed, voting closed now or reopened. Last, cancelling the event. The lists of links and of emails share the stylesheet partial `_wells.scss` (`apps/web/src/styles`): white wells, each with its name over a line and its actions beside them.

**Components:**

A browser with no management link of the event and no live session (`Management` `signIn`, on opening or after any request) goes to `/sign-in` with `signInFrom` (`apps/web/src/app/core/auth`), replacing the entry in the history, and signing in comes back to the page; one whose link does not manage the event sees "No tienes acceso a este evento" (focus on its heading), a cancelled event (`410`, or after cancelling) the cancelled `VoteEnded` (`apps/web/src/app/features/vote`) with, inside it, "Avisa al grupo con este mensaje:", the message `Se ha cancelado "{title}".` and `ShareLinks` without a link, every time the page opens; only a failed request offers to try again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

The usual case (voting closed, a recommended option, votes in) is confirmed at once; otherwise a question (`Dialog`, `apps/web/src/app/shared/ui`) first says why it is unusual (`confirmationNotes`, `packages/domain/src`: nobody voted; nobody can attend any option; not the recommended option, naming them; voting will close) and that the confirmation is final. Once confirmed: the green card with the date in full (`optionInFull`), always in sight (not a section), focused when the organizer has just confirmed.
