### `packages/contracts/src/auth`

**Summary:** The sign-in, sign-out, session and account deletion endpoints.

**Purpose:** `POST /api/auth/sign-in-code` sends a 6-digit code to an email; `POST /api/auth/sign-in` signs the browser in with it, creating the account if the email has none, and says where an application's request to connect that opened the sign-in page goes on; `POST /api/auth/sign-out` deletes the browser's session on the server, then clears its cookies; `GET /api/auth/session` tells a page which account its browser is signed in as; `POST /api/me/deletion-code` sends the signed-in account's email a code and `POST /api/me/deletion` deletes the account and all its events with it. Also the refusal of a session sent from a page of another site, shared by every change a session can make, and the connector's path (`connectorPath`). Emails are trimmed and compared in lower case.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `sendSignInCodeEndpoint` (`sign-in.ts`)                                              | The endpoint that sends a code: `200` delivered, `400` a broken body, `403` from another site or without `Origin`, `429` too many codes (per email: a new one after 30 seconds, at most 5 an hour; per address), `502` not delivered.                              |
| `signInCodeBodySchema`, `SignInCodeBody` (`sign-in.ts`)                              | Its body `{ email }` (at most 254 characters).                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `signInCodeSentSchema`, `SignInCodeSent` (`sign-in.ts`)                              | Its answer `{ sent: true, resendAfterSeconds }`: the new code replaces the last one, valid for 10 minutes and 5 wrong tries.                                                                                                                                       |
| `codeNotDeliveredSchema`, `CodeNotDeliveredBody` (`sign-in.ts`)                      | `502 CODE_NOT_DELIVERED`: the email server did not take the email; asking again sends a new code.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `signInEndpoint` (`sign-in.ts`)                                                      | The endpoint that signs in: `200` with the session cookie (and where the browser goes on, when the sign-in carried a request to connect), `400` refused, `403` from another site, `429` too many tries from the address, `500`.                                    |
| `signInBodySchema`, `SignInBody` (`sign-in.ts`)                                      | Its body `{ email, code, name?, connectionRequest? }`, the code being 6 digits; `name`, trimmed, is the one an account created by this sign-in takes; `connectionRequest` is the query of the sign-in page's address, whole and as it is, when an application's request to connect opened the page: the request as the authorization server signed it, valid for 10 minutes. |
| `signedInSchema`, `SignedIn` (`sign-in.ts`)                                          | Its answer `{ signedIn: true, continueTo? }`. `continueTo` comes only when the sign-in carried a request to connect: the path of qando's own site the browser opens next, with a whole navigation. It is the authorization server's address with what the application asked, which takes the request again now that there is a session; or the consent page's (`/connect`) without a request, to start again from the application, when the request is older than 10 minutes or is not one the authorization server signed. |
| `wrongCodeSchema`, `codeExpiredSchema`, `tooManyAttemptsSchema` (`sign-in.ts`)       | The refusals of a code: `WRONG_CODE` with `attemptsLeft` (1 to 4), `CODE_EXPIRED` (expired, used, or never sent), `TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS` (void after 5 wrong tries, even for the right code).                                                                         |
| `signInRefusedSchema`, `SignInRefusedBody` (`sign-in.ts`)                            | Every `400` of signing in: those three or `VALIDATION_FAILED`.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `signOutEndpoint` (`sign-out.ts`)                                                    | The endpoint: `200` signed out, `403` the session from another site, `500` the session could not be deleted (its cookie kept).                                                                                                                                     |
| `signedOutSchema`, `SignedOut` (`sign-out.ts`)                                       | The answer `{ signedOut: true }`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `crossSiteSessionSchema`, `CrossSiteSessionBody` (`sign-out.ts`)                     | `403 FORBIDDEN` to a change sent with the session from a page of another site, or without `Origin` (CSRF).                                                                                                                                                         |
| `sessionEndpoint` (`session.ts`)                                                     | `GET /api/auth/session`, answered to anyone, as every page asks it: `200` the account of the browser's session or `null` without one (never `401`), `500` the session could not be read.                                                                           |
| `signedInAccountSchema`, `SignedInAccount` (`session.ts`)                            | Its answer `{ name, email }`: the account the browser is signed in as; `name` is empty until the account creates its first event or names itself.                                                                                                                  |
| `sendDeletionCodeEndpoint` (`account-deletion.ts`)                                   | The endpoint that sends the code that deletes the signed-in account, without a body: `200` delivered, `401` without a session, `403` from another site, `429` too many codes (a new one after 30 seconds, 5 an hour, and per address), `500`, `502` not delivered. |
| `deletionCodeSentSchema`, `DeletionCodeSent` (`account-deletion.ts`)                 | Its answer `{ sent: true, resendAfterSeconds }`: the email's one code, the one signing in takes too, valid for 10 minutes and 5 wrong tries.                                                                                                                       |
| `deleteAccountEndpoint` (`account-deletion.ts`)                                      | The endpoint that deletes the signed-in account with the code: `200` deleted and the cookies cleared, `400` refused, `401`, `403`, `429` too many tries from the address, `500`.                                                                                   |
| `accountDeletionBodySchema`, `AccountDeletionBody` (`account-deletion.ts`)           | Its body `{ code }`, 6 digits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `accountDeletedSchema`, `AccountDeleted` (`account-deletion.ts`)                     | Its answer `{ deleted: true, events }`: the account, its events with everything under them and what is left of the events it cancelled are deleted; `events` counts the events deleted, not the cancelled ones.                                                    |
| `accountDeletionRefusedSchema`, `AccountDeletionRefusedBody` (`account-deletion.ts`) | Why nothing was deleted: a broken body, `WRONG_CODE` with `attemptsLeft`, `CODE_EXPIRED` or `TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS`, as for signing in.                                                                                                                                |
| `connectingApplicationEndpoint` (`connecting-application.ts`) | The endpoint the consent page asks which application a request to connect names: `200` the application, `400` a broken body, `401` without a session, `403` from a page of another site or without `Origin`, `410` a request that expired or that the authorization server did not sign, `429` too many requests from the address, `500`. |
| `connectingApplicationBodySchema`, `ConnectingApplicationBody` (`connecting-application.ts`) | Its body `{ connectionRequest }`: the query of the consent page's address, whole and as it is. |
| `connectingApplicationSchema`, `ConnectingApplication` (`connecting-application.ts`) | Its answer `{ name, host }`: the name the application gives itself and the host of the address its document is published at; never its logo. |
| `connectionRequestExpiredSchema`, `ConnectionRequestExpiredBody` (`connecting-application.ts`) | The `410` body, `CONNECTION_REQUEST_EXPIRED`: nothing to allow, the person starts again from the application. |
| `connectorPath` (`connected-applications.ts`) | Where the connector answers, `/api/mcp`: the API serves the connector there (`apps/api/src/modules/connector`) and issues access tokens for it (`apps/api/src/modules/auth`), and "Apps conectadas" gives it, after the page's origin, as the address to connect an assistant to (`apps/web/src/app/features/connected-apps`). |
| `connectedApplicationsEndpoint` (`connected-applications.ts`) | The endpoint "Apps conectadas" reads the account's applications from, `GET /api/me/connected-apps`: `200` the list, `401` without a session, `500`. |
| `connectedApplicationSchema`, `ConnectedApplication` (`connected-applications.ts`) | One application `{ id, name, host, connectedAt }`: the connection, which disconnecting names (what the account allowed, new each time the application is connected again); the name and the host as the consent page shows them; and when the account allowed it. |
| `connectedApplicationsSchema` (`connected-applications.ts`) | The list, the newest connection first, maybe empty. |
| `disconnectApplicationEndpoint` (`connected-applications.ts`) | The endpoint that disconnects one, `DELETE /api/me/connected-apps/{id}`: `200`, `400` a connection that breaks the contract, `401` without a session, `403` the session sent from a page of another site, `404` a connection the account does not have (never connected, disconnected already, or another account's), `500`. |
| `connectionParamsSchema` (`connected-applications.ts`) | Its path `{ id }`: the connection as the list gives it, 1 to 64 characters. |
| `disconnectedSchema`, `Disconnected` (`connected-applications.ts`) | Its `200`, `{ disconnected: true }`: the application's next call and its next renewal are refused. |
| `connectionNotFoundSchema`, `ConnectionNotFoundBody` (`connected-applications.ts`) | Its `404` body, `NOT_FOUND`. |

**Depends on:** `packages/contracts/src`.

**Used by:** `apps/api/src/http`, `apps/api/src/modules/auth`, `apps/api/src/modules/connector`, `apps/web/src/app/core/auth`, `apps/web/src/app/core/layout`, `apps/web/src/app/features/connect`, `apps/web/src/app/features/connected-apps`.

### `packages/contracts/src/date-interpretations`

**Summary:** The endpoint that reads a date phrase.

**Purpose:** `POST /api/date-interpretations` reads the dates and times of a phrase in plain language, for the page that creates an event to mark: nothing is stored, and every phrase gets an answer (what is not understood comes as notices, never as an error). Only qando's pages may send it, at most 20 phrases in any hour per address. The answer has the shape of what `readDates` of `packages/date-reader` answers, written here as schemas so that the contract depends on no other package; dates and times carry no zone.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                              | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dateInterpretationEndpoint` (`date-interpretation.ts`)                             | The endpoint: `200` what the phrase says, `400` a broken body, `403` from a page of another site or without `Origin`, `429` too many phrases from the address, `500`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `dateInterpretationBodySchema`, `DateInterpretationBody` (`date-interpretation.ts`) | Its body `{ text, timeZone, region? }`, nothing else: the phrase (1 to 120 characters once trimmed), the IANA name of the time zone it is written in (one the runtime knows; today and the time now are taken in it) and the region of the browser's language (two capital letters: `ES`, `US`), which orders a date in figures; any other text is read as no region, never refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `dateInterpretationSchema`, `DateInterpretation` (`date-interpretation.ts`)         | Its answer `{ options, questions, notices, timesLeftOut, questionsNotAsked }`, each in the phrase's order, as an event can hold it. An option is a day or a range of days with a time (`single`, `range` of the same day, `question` with the place of its question in `questions`) or `null` for whole days. A question is `{ fragment, dates, morning, afternoon, leftOut? }`: both readings of a time whose half of the day was not said, of which an event can hold one at least; `leftOut` names the one it cannot (a range within one clock hour), which marks its days whole when picked. A notice is `{ kind, fragment, dates }` for `timeUnclear` and `tooLate`, the same with `written` (`weekday` or `date`) for `dayNotWritten`, `{ kind, fragment? }` for `unclear`, `mismatch`, `past` and `horizon`, `{ kind, fragment }` for `pastTime` (a time of today already past), and `{ kind }` for `tooMany`. A time left out is `{ time, dates }`: a range no event can hold (within one clock hour, or with `nextDay` when it ends on the day after) and every day it was said of. A question not asked is a question's `{ fragment, dates, morning, afternoon }`, both readings ranges no event can hold. |

### `packages/contracts/src/management`

**Summary:** Creating an event, the endpoints opened with a management token, and the signed-in account's events.

**Purpose:** Creating an event with the session (`POST /api/events`, not rate-limited of its own), and what the organizer can do with the management link, the token sent in `X-Management-Token` (22 to 64 base64url characters; optional, since the session will be the other way in). Reading the event to manage it, with the facts a decision needs (how many voted, which options are recommended), confirming its final option and retrying a failed email to the organizer. ### `packages/date-reader`

**Summary:** Reads dates written in plain language (`@qando/date-reader`).

**Purpose:** Turns what an organizer types to say when an event could take place ("todos los lunes de julio a las 20:30") into the date and time options to review, in Spanish, Catalan and English. It reads by rules alone, as a pure function with no input or output: no library, no service to call, and the same phrase on the same day always gives the same answer. The two limits of an event's options, how many and how far ahead, are the domain's (`packages/domain`), so the reader never proposes what an event would refuse. Its evaluation set runs with the unit tests and fails them below the agreed score, 100 %. It also judges whether a phrase copy-edited by someone else still says when as the original does (the edit check), with the same words and tokens it reads with. The API uses the edit check; nothing calls the reader yet.

**Contents:** `src/`; package, TypeScript, Vitest and Stryker settings (mutation threshold 85 %; the word lists of the languages are data and are not mutated; CI runs it in five parallel parts, `STRYKER_PART`: the two halves of `src/phrase-reader.ts`, `src/tokenizer.ts`, `src/calendar.ts` and the other files).

**Depends on:** `packages/domain`.

**Used by:** `apps/api`.

### `packages/date-reader/src`

**Summary:** The reader, its grammar and calendar, the check of an edit, and the evaluation set.

**Purpose:** The package has two public functions, exported by `index.ts`: **`readDates`**, with the types of its answer, and **`keepsWhen`**, the check of an edit; everything else is internal to the package and may change without notice. A phrase is read in three steps: the tokenizer (`tokenizer.ts`) cuts it into tokens with the vocabulary; the grammar (`phrase-reader.ts`) turns the tokens into a reading, what the phrase names as said, with no calendar arithmetic; the calendar (`calendar.ts`) turns the reading into options counted from today, with the questions and the notices; the reading keeps where each fragment starts in the phrase, which is what the order of the answer goes by. The grammar never names a word, so a new synonym or language is rows in `vocabulary/` and a case in the evaluation set. The reading rules (`R1`…`R34`) are written in `evaluation-set.json`, and the comments of the code name the one they apply. The check of an edit (`edit-check.ts`) compares how two phrases are written, the organizer's and its copy edit, with the tokenizer and the vocabulary, and never works out a date; the words it needs beyond the grammar's are data of each language too.

**Contents:** `vocabulary/`; the files below; `evaluation-set.json`, the 687 cases of the evaluation set with the reading rules, kept as written (Prettier leaves it alone); `evaluation-set.test.ts`, which runs every case and fails below 100 %, and checks that the options of every answer pass the domain's `validateOptions` (all but those whose time is still a question or ends on the day after).

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `readDates(text, { today, now, region })` (`read-dates.ts`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | **The public interface.** Reads a date phrase written on `today` (YYYY-MM-DD, the day every relative date counts from) and answers `{ options, questions, notices }`, each in the phrase's order: the options to mark, one question per distinct time whose half of the day was not said, and one notice per fragment, every one that applies. `now` (HH:MM, optional) is the time of day: the earlier times of today are past, not marked and told (`pastTime`), and a bare hour whose morning has passed is its afternoon, with no question. `region` (the browser's, optional) makes a date in figures month/day for "US" and day/month otherwise. Every phrase gets an answer, never an error. It never guesses: what it cannot read is told in a notice with its fragment and never becomes an option, and so is a date that does not exist, is past or is more than 12 months away. A phrase that adds up to more than 60 options, or of which nothing is understood, marks nothing and gives one notice alone; one whose only content does not fit, is past or is too far gives the notice of each fragment. A day said twice is one option, and a whole day gives way to the same day with a time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `keepsWhen(original, edited)` (`edit-check.ts`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | **Public: the check of an edit.** Whether a copy-edited phrase still says when as the phrase the organizer wrote; `false` means the edit may read as other dates or times and must be discarded. The edit writes no number the original did not, counted as many times as written there (a number in words is the same number in figures; "00" minutes and leading zeros add nothing; "a esa misma hora" lets it write an hour again); an edit that drops a day of the month or an hour still says one of its kind, as a correction does ("el sábado a las 10, no, a las 11" → "el sábado a las 11" passes); the weekdays keep their order and none is new (a weekend said alone is never split into its two days); the only month named stays, and no month is new ("julio o agosto" → "junio o agosto" is discarded); no "today", "tomorrow" or "day after tomorrow" is new ("tomorrow at 8" → "today at 8" is discarded); a date negation stays or goes with the date it rules out; a week or month reference stays unless every day left has its day number; a half of the day is still settled when the original settles one, and the edit settles none the original does not ("Friday at 8" → "Friday at 8pm" is discarded, so the reader asks which half), says a half of no more hours than the times the original settles it, and gives no hour another half than the one said beside it ("Friday at 8am or Saturday at 9pm" → "Friday at 8pm or Saturday at 9am" is discarded); each meal word keeps a word of the same meaning. Only the original is read as a person reads it: a number word or a weekday with a typo, glued, split or shortened counts as written, and so does a half word with a typo, glued, split or in one of its listed short forms ("noxe", "porlatarde", "medio dia", "mñn"), though never a word the vocabulary already reads as something else ("mañana" alone is tomorrow); a month word with a typo and the month of a feast say their month, and a day word in a listed short form, with a typo or glued says its day ("mñn", "pasao mañna", "lunchtmrw"). It needs no "today" and never throws. |
| `DatesRead`, `ReadOption`, `ReadDates`, `ReadTime`, `ClockTime`, `TimeQuestion`, `ReadNotice`, `NoticeKind` (`dates-read.ts`)                                                                                                                                                                           | **Public:** the types of the answer. Dates are calendar values (YYYY-MM-DD) and times clock values (HH:MM), with no zone. An option is a day or a range of days with a time (`single`, `range` with `nextDay` when it ends on the day after, `question` with the place of its question) or none. A question is `{ fragment, dates, morning, afternoon }`. A notice is `{ kind, fragment, dates }` for `timeUnclear` and `tooLate` (`dates`: the first day of each option the fragment speaks of; none for a vague time said of no day), the same with `written` (`weekday` or `date`: how the phrase wrote the day) for `dayNotWritten`, `{ kind, fragment? }` for `unclear`, `mismatch`, `past` and `horizon` (no fragment when it speaks of the whole phrase), `{ kind, fragment }` for `pastTime` (a time of today already past; `past` is a date) and `{ kind }` for `tooMany`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `read(text, region)` (`phrase-reader.ts`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Internal: the grammar. Reads a phrase into its reading.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `resolve(reading, today, now)` (`calendar.ts`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Internal: the calendar. The answer a reading gives on a day: its options, questions and notices in the phrase's order; all the arithmetic and every rule that needs "today".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `tokenize(text, region)`, `plain(word)`, `nearlyEqual(a, b)`, `isYear(year)`, `Token`, `TokenType` (`tokenizer.ts`)                                                                                                                                                                                     | Internal: the tokens of a phrase in order, each with its place in it; `isYear` says whether a number can be the year of a date (2000 to 2100; a year in figures outside them is read as the nearest); a word of four letters or more that is one letter away from a word of the vocabulary of five or more is read as that word, and a figure glued to letters is one word when the vocabulary lists it so ("2nite"). `plain` writes a word as the vocabulary does, in lower case and without accents; `nearlyEqual` says whether two words are the same or one letter apart (one changed, added, dropped, or two neighbours swapped).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### `packages/date-reader/src/vocabulary`

**Summary:** The words of each language.

**Purpose:** Every word the date reader knows, as data: one file per language, each row a term and the phrases that mean it, written in lower case, without accents and with single spaces. `vocabulary.ts` merges them into the one lookup the tokenizer uses. Internal to the package. The order of the rows matters to a mistyped word one letter away from several words, which is read as the first of them: the lookup keeps the phrases by kind of term, then language by language as written.

**Exports:**

| Export                                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vocabulary()` (`vocabulary.ts`)               | Every phrase of every language with the term it means, built on first use and kept. A phrase listed in several languages means the same in each.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `wordsThatAreNotTypos()` (`vocabulary.ts`)     | The words that look like a typo of a vocabulary word and are not ("vienes" is not "viernes"), never read as one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `chatShorthand()` (`vocabulary.ts`)            | The short forms of chat of every language, each with the word the tokenizer reads it as ("xa" is "para", "tb" is "también"), built on first use and kept.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `editWords()` (`vocabulary.ts`)                | The words of the check of an edit, those of every language together, built on first use and kept.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `EditWords` (`term.ts`)                        | The words the check of an edit reads beyond the grammar's terms, as lists: minutes said in words with their number ("y media"), the word that joins tens and units ("treinta y uno") or a ten and its units ("diez y ocho"), what a person reads as a number where it stands ("veinti cinco", the Catalan "el u"), what chat glues before a month ("doct"), the words that after "no" correct the phrase ("no, perdón"), those that deny a date as "no" does ("tampoco"), the ways of saying one cannot ("can't"), the words of a span ("todo julio") the words that say a half of the day, each with its half and the short ways chat writes it ("mañana": "mñn"), the words that say a day counted from today, each with its short forms ("tomorrow": "tmrw", "tmr"), and the words that alone say the day after once tomorrow is said ("mañana y si no pasado"). |
| `Term`, `TermType`, `Language` (`term.ts`)     | What a phrase means to the grammar: its kind (a weekday, a month, a number, "every", "except"…) and what that kind needs (a value, the half of the day…); the words of one language, as rows of a term and its phrases, with its words of the check of an edit (`edits`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `es` (`es.ts`), `ca` (`ca.ts`), `en` (`en.ts`) | The words of Spanish, Catalan and English.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `shared` (`shared.ts`)                         | What the three languages write the same way: symbols (`&`, `+`, `@`) and short forms (`h`, `am`, `pm`, `ok`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

**Depends on:** `packages/date-reader/src` (the type of the half of the day, `reading.ts`).

**Used by:** `packages/date-reader/src`.

### `packages/domain`

**Summary:** Business rules (`@qando/domain`).

**Purpose:** The rules the API and the web must apply the same way, as pure functions with no input or output. The API enforces them; the web uses them to tell the participant about a problem before sending.

**Contents:** `src/`; package, TypeScript, Vitest and Stryker settings (mutation threshold 85 %).

**Depends on:** —

**Used by:** `apps/api`, `apps/web`, `packages/date-reader`.

### `packages/domain/src`

**Summary:** Event details, option rules, event state, vote rules, results and what confirming a date is decided from.

**Purpose:** What makes the name and title of a new event valid, which lists of options it can have (how many, how far ahead, which ranges and times, none alike) and their order, what makes a whole new event valid, when an event accepts votes, what makes a vote valid, what the votes amount to, and what confirming a date is decided from (its facts and the notes of the question before it). `index.ts` re-exports `event-details.ts`, `options.ts`, `event-state.ts`, `vote.ts`, `results.ts`, `new-event.ts`, `deadline.ts` and `decision.ts`.

**Exports:**

| Export                                                                                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `detailsProblems(details)`, `organizerNameProblem(name)`, `titleProblem(title)` (`event-details.ts`)                                    | Every problem of an organizer's name and an event's title, the name's first, each measured once trimmed: missing (empty or only spaces), name too short (one character) or too long, title too long; none when an event can be created with them; `organizerNameProblem` is the name's alone (the wizard's last step), also the rule of the name a new account takes when signing in, and `titleProblem` the title's alone (the wizard's step 1).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ORGANIZER_NAME_MIN_LENGTH`, `ORGANIZER_NAME_MAX_LENGTH`, `EVENT_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH` (`event-details.ts`)          | The limits, 2 and 30 for the name, 50 for the title.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `EventDetails`, `DetailsProblem` (`event-details.ts`)                                                            | The name and title as typed, and each problem's code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `MAX_OPTIONS` (`options.ts`)                                                                                     | The most options an event can have, 60; each date, range of dates or time proposed is one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `latestOptionDate(today)` (`options.ts`)                                                                         | The last day an event created on `today` can propose: the same day twelve months later (28 February after a 29 February); both as `YYYY-MM-DD`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

| `onQuarter(time)` (`options.ts`) | Whether a clock time (`HH:MM`) is on a quarter of its hour, :00, :15, :30 or :45, the only minutes an option's time can have (`validateOptions` answers `TIME_OFF_QUARTER` otherwise); the connector uses it to name the time that is off the quarters, a range's start or, when the start is on one, its end. |

Options may overlap. The order: by first day, then by when they start, an option without a time counting from 0:00; a day or a time before a range that starts with it; ranges of days by their last day, then time ranges by their end. Dates and times must be well formed (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `HH:MM`). |

| `validateVote(event, input)` (`vote.ts`)                                                                         | Checks a vote against its event and answers `{ status: 'valid', vote }` (name trimmed), `{ status: 'invalid', problems }` with every problem at once (name too short or too long, name on an anonymous event, option missing, more than one preferred), or `{ status: 'other-options' }` when it answers an option the event does not have (the options were replaced).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
